translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 148
translations.idiomatic: Volume 148 of the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance

sentences.zh: 【梁紀四】　起旃蒙協洽，盡著雍閹茂，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 4] Beginning in the year Jimeng-Xiehe and ending in Zhuyong-Yanmao, four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 4] Covering four years, from 515 through 518 CE.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝四天監十四年（

translations.literal: The fourteenth year of Tianjian of Emperor Wu of Liang (
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianjian of Emperor Wu of Liang (

sentences.zh: 乙未，公元五一五年）

translations.literal: yimao, corresponding to the year 515 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yimao, or 515 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙巳朔，上冠太子於太極殿，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the first day of the month (yisi), the Emperor performed the capping ceremony for the Crown Prince in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, the Emperor crowned the Crown Prince in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Emperor sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Emperor performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，魏主有疾；

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Wei sovereign fell ill;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Northern Wei emperor fell ill;

sentences.zh: 丁巳，殂於式乾殿。

translations.literal: On dingsi, he died in the Shigan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, he died in the Shigan Hall.

sentences.zh: 侍中、中書監、太子少傅催光，侍中、領軍將軍於忠，詹事王顯，中庶子代人侯剛，迎太子詡於東宮，至顯陽殿。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Cui Guang; Palace Attendant and General of the Palace Guards Yu Zhong; Household Steward Wang Xian; and Attendant of the Heir Apparent Hou Gang of the Dai people went to the Eastern Palace to welcome Crown Prince Xu and brought him to the Xianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang, who served as palace attendant, director of the Secretariat, and junior tutor to the Crown Prince; Yu Zhong, palace attendant and general of the palace guards; Wang Xian, household steward; and Hou Gang of Dai, attendant of the heir apparent, went to the Eastern Palace to escort Crown Prince Xu to the Xianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 王顯欲須明行即位禮，崔光曰：「天位不可暫曠，何待至明！

translations.literal: Wang Xian wished to wait until dawn to perform the enthronement rites. Cui Guang said, "The throne cannot be left vacant even briefly—why wait until dawn!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian wanted to wait for daylight before holding the enthronement ceremony. Cui Guang said, "The throne cannot stand empty even for a moment—why wait until morning!

sentences.zh: 」顯曰：「須奏中宮。

translations.literal: " Xian said, "We must report to the empress in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xian said, "We must first inform the empress dowager in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「帝崩，太子立，國之常典，何須中宮令也！

translations.literal: " Guang said, "When the emperor dies, the crown prince succeeds—this is the regular statute of the state. Why need an order from the inner palace!
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Guang replied, "When an emperor dies, the crown prince ascends the throne—that is the established law of the realm. What need is there for an order from the inner palace!

sentences.zh: 」於是光等請太子止哭，立於東序；

translations.literal: " Thereupon Guang and the others asked the crown prince to cease mourning and stand on the eastern side of the hall;
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Cui Guang and his colleagues asked the crown prince to stop wailing and took their places on the east side of the hall;

sentences.zh: 於忠與黃門郎元昭扶太子西面哭十餘聲：「止。

translations.literal: Yu Zhong and the Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Zhao supported the crown prince, who faced west and wailed more than ten times; then they said, "Stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong and Yuan Zhao, a Yellow Gate attendant, supported the crown prince as he faced west and wept a dozen times before they called out, "Enough.

sentences.zh: 光攝太尉，奉策進璽綬，太子跪受，服袞冕之服，御太極殿，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Guang acted as regent Grand Commandant, presented the edict and advanced the imperial seal and cord; the crown prince knelt to receive them, donned the robe and cap of state, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and took the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as regent grand commandant, Cui Guang presented the edict of succession and offered the imperial seal and cord. The crown prince knelt to receive them, put on the robes and crown of state, entered the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 光等與夜直群官立庭中，北面稽首稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Guang and the other officials on night duty in the palace stood in the courtyard, faced north, bowed to the ground, and shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang and the other officials on night duty in the palace stood in the courtyard, faced north, kowtowed, and shouted their acclamation.

sentences.zh: 昭，遵之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhao was a great-grandson of Yuan Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhao was a great-grandson of Yuan Zun.

sentences.zh: 高後欲殺胡貴嬪，中給事譙郡劉騰以告侯剛，剛以告於忠。

translations.literal: Empress Gao wished to kill Honored Consort Hu. The Central Palace Attendant Liu Teng of Qiao commandery informed Hou Gang, and Gang informed Yu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gao wanted to kill Honored Consort Hu. Liu Teng of Qiao, a central palace attendant, told Hou Gang, who in turn told Yu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠問計於崔光，光使置貴嬪於別所，嚴加守衛，由是貴嬪深德四人。

translations.literal: Zhong asked Cui Guang for a plan. Guang had the honored consort placed in a separate residence and strictly guarded. Because of this the honored consort was deeply grateful to the four men.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong asked Cui Guang what to do. Guang had the honored consort moved to a separate residence and placed under strict guard. The honored consort thereafter felt deep gratitude toward the four men.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the Northern Wei court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己未，悉召西伐、東防兵。

translations.literal: On jiwei, all troops on the western campaign and eastern defense were summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the court recalled all troops engaged in the western campaign and eastern defense.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍廣平王懷扶疾入臨，逕至太極西廡，哀慟，呼侍中、黃門、領軍、二衛，云：「身欲上殿哭大行，又須入見主上。

translations.literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Prince of Guangping Yuan Huai, supporting himself in illness, came to mourn and went straight to the western corridor of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. Grieving deeply, he called to the palace attendants, Yellow Gate officials, commander of the palace guards, and the two guard corps, saying, "I wish to ascend the hall to mourn the late emperor, and I must also enter to see the new sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huai, Prince of Guangping and grand general of agile cavalry, came to mourn despite his illness and went straight to the western corridor of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. Deep in grief, he summoned the palace attendants, Yellow Gate officials, commander of the palace guards, and the two guard corps and said, "I mean to go up to the hall to mourn the late emperor, and I must also enter to see the new sovereign.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆愕然相視，無敢對者。

translations.literal: " All were startled and looked at one another; none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone stared at one another in dismay, and no one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 崔光攘衰振杖，引漢光武崩趙熹扶諸王下殿故事，聲色甚厲，聞者莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Cui Guang pushed aside his mourning garment and shook his staff, citing the precedent of Zhao Xi escorting the princes down from the hall when Emperor Guangwu of Han died. His voice and bearing were very stern; all who heard praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang threw back his mourning robe and struck his staff, citing the precedent of Zhao Xi escorting the princes down from the hall at the death of Emperor Guangwu of Han. His voice and manner were fiercely stern, and all who heard him approved.

sentences.zh: 懷聲淚俱止，曰：「侍中以古義裁我，我敢不服？

translations.literal: Huai's voice and tears both ceased. He said, "The palace attendant has judged me by ancient precedent—how dare I not submit?
translations.idiomatic: Huai fell silent and stopped weeping. He said, "The palace attendant has rebuked me with ancient precedent—how could I refuse to obey?

sentences.zh: 」遂還，仍頻遣左右致謝。

translations.literal: " He then withdrew, and repeatedly sent attendants to express his thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " He withdrew, and repeatedly sent attendants to thank Cui Guang.

sentences.zh: 先是，高肇擅權，尤忌宗室有時望者。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gao Zhao had monopolized power and especially resented members of the imperial clan who enjoyed reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gao Zhao had monopolized power and was especially wary of imperial clansmen who enjoyed public esteem.

sentences.zh: 太子太保任城王澄數為肇所譖，懼不自全，乃終日酣飲，所為如狂，朝廷機要無所關豫。

translations.literal: The heir apparent's grand guardian, Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, had several times been slandered by Zhao. Fearing he could not preserve himself, he drank heavily all day long and behaved as if mad, taking no part in the court's vital affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng and grand guardian to the heir apparent, had been slandered by Gao Zhao on several occasions. Fearing for his life, he drank heavily all day and acted like a madman, taking no part in the court's vital affairs.

sentences.zh: 及世宗殂，肇擁兵於外，朝野不安。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, Zhao held troops outside the capital, and court and countryside were uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Gao Zhao held troops outside the capital, and unease spread through court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 於忠與門下議，以肅宗幼，未能親政，宜使太保高陽王雍入居西柏堂省決庶政，以任城王澄為尚書令，總攝百揆，奏皇后請即敕授。

translations.literal: Yu Zhong discussed with the Secretariat that, because Emperor Suzong was young and unable to rule in person, the grand guardian Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong should enter the Western Cypress Hall to decide routine administration, and Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng should be made Director of the Imperial Secretariat to oversee all ministries. They memorialized the empress to issue immediate edicts of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong conferred with the Secretariat. Because the new emperor Xiaoming was still a child and could not rule in person, they proposed that Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang and grand guardian, should take up residence in the Western Cypress Hall to decide routine administration, and that Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, should be made director of the Imperial Secretariat to oversee all ministries. They memorialized the empress to issue immediate edicts of appointment.

sentences.zh: 王顯素有寵於世宗，恃勢使威，為世所疾，恐不為澄等所容，與中常侍孫伏連等密謀寢門下之奏，矯皇后令，以高肇錄尚書事，以顯與勃海公高猛同為侍中。

translations.literal: Wang Xian had long enjoyed favor under Emperor Shizong. Relying on his power he threw his weight about and was resented by the world. Fearing he would not be tolerated by Cheng and the others, he secretly plotted with the Central Regular Attendant Sun Fulian and others to suppress the Secretariat's memorial, forged an order from the empress, and appointed Gao Zhao to oversee the Imperial Secretariat, with Xian and the Duke of Bohai Gao Meng both made palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian had long enjoyed Emperor Xuanwu's favor and abused his power until he was widely hated. Fearing he would not be tolerated by Yuan Cheng and his allies, he secretly plotted with Sun Fulian, a central regular attendant, and others to suppress the Secretariat's memorial, forged an order from the empress, appointed Gao Zhao to oversee the Imperial Secretariat, and made both himself and Gao Meng, Duke of Bohai, palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 於忠等聞之，托以侍療無效，執顯於禁中，下詔削爵任。

translations.literal: When Yu Zhong and the others heard of this, they used the pretext that his attendance in nursing the emperor had been ineffective, seized Xian inside the palace, and issued an edict stripping him of his fief and office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Zhong and his allies learned of this, they seized Wang Xian inside the palace on the pretext that his nursing of the late emperor had been ineffective, and issued an edict stripping him of his fief and office.

sentences.zh: 顯臨執呼冤，直閣以刀鐶撞其掖下，送右衛府，一宿而死。

translations.literal: As he was seized Xian cried that he was wronged. A duty officer in the inner apartments struck him under the arm with a sword guard and sent him to the Right Guard Office; after one night he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: As he was seized, Wang Xian protested his innocence. A duty officer in the inner apartments struck him under the arm with a sword guard and sent him to the Right Guard Office, where he died within a night.

sentences.zh: 庚申，下詔如門下所奏，百官總己聽於二王，中外悅服。

translations.literal: On gengshen, an edict was issued as the Secretariat had memorialized. All officials entrusted themselves to the two princes, and within and without the court were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, an edict was issued along the lines the Secretariat had proposed. All officials placed themselves under the two princes' authority, and court and countryside alike were reassured.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚辰，尊皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengchen, the empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengchen, the empress was elevated to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 魏主稱名為書告哀於高肇，且召之還。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign wrote a letter of mourning to Gao Zhao using his personal name and also summoned him to return.
translations.idiomatic: The new Wei emperor wrote a letter of condolence to Gao Zhao using his personal name and summoned him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 肇承變憂懼，朝夕哭泣，至於羸悴。

translations.literal: Zhao, learning of the change, was anxious and fearful. He wept morning and evening until he was emaciated and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao learned of the emperor's death, he was stricken with fear and wept morning and night until he was gaunt and haggard.

sentences.zh: 歸至瀍澗，家人迎之，不與相見。

translations.literal: When he returned to Chanjian, his family came to meet him, but he would not see them.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chanjian, his family came out to meet him, but he refused to see them.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，至闕下，衰服號哭，升太極殿盡哀。

translations.literal: On xinsi, he arrived below the palace gates, wailed in mourning garments, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and expressed his full grief.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, he arrived at the palace gates in mourning dress, wailing loudly, then ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to perform his full mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍與於忠密謀，伏直寢邢豹等十餘人於舍人省下，肇哭畢，引入西廡，清河諸王皆竊言目之。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong and Yu Zhong secretly plotted and stationed more than ten men on night duty in the inner apartments, including Xing Bao, in ambush below the Attendants' Office. When Zhao had finished mourning, they led him into the western corridor. The princes of Qinghe all whispered and watched him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, and Yu Zhong secretly stationed more than ten men on night duty in the inner apartments, including Xing Bao, in ambush below the Attendants' Office. When Gao Zhao had finished mourning, they led him into the western corridor while the princes of Qinghe watched and whispered among themselves.

sentences.zh: 肇入省，豹等扼殺之，下詔暴其罪惡，稱肇自盡，自餘親黨悉無所問，削除職爵，葬以士禮；

translations.literal: Zhao entered the office; Bao and the others strangled him. An edict exposed his crimes and said Zhao had killed himself. The rest of his kin and associates were not questioned. His offices and titles were removed, and he was buried with the rites due a common gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao entered the office, Bao and the others strangled him. An edict exposed his crimes and claimed he had taken his own life. The rest of his kin and associates were not prosecuted. His offices and titles were stripped away, and he was buried with the rites due a common gentleman;

sentences.zh: 逮昏，於廁門出屍歸其家。

translations.literal: at dusk his corpse was taken out through the privy gate and returned to his family.
translations.idiomatic: at dusk his corpse was taken out through the privy gate and sent back to his family.

sentences.zh: 魏之伐蜀也，軍至晉壽，蜀人震恐。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Shu, its army reached Jinshou and the people of Shu were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Wei campaign against Shu, the Wei army reached Jinshou and threw the Shu forces into panic.

sentences.zh: 傅豎眼將步兵三萬擊巴北，上遣寧州刺史任太洪自陰平間道入其州，招誘氐、蜀，絕魏運路。

translations.literal: Fu Shuyan led thirty thousand infantry to strike northern Ba. The Emperor sent the Inspector of Ningzhou Ren Taihong by the hidden route of Yinping into that province to win over the Di and Shu peoples and cut off Wei's supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan led thirty thousand foot soldiers against northern Ba. The Liang emperor sent Ren Taihong, inspector of Ningzhou, through the hidden route of Yinping into the region to win over the Di and Shu peoples and sever the Wei supply lines.

sentences.zh: 會魏大軍北還，太洪襲破魏東洛、除口二戍，聲言梁兵繼至，氐、蜀翕然從之。

translations.literal: As the great Wei army returned north, Taihong raided and broke the two garrisons of Dongluo and Chukou, proclaiming that Liang troops were following close behind. The Di and Shu submitted to him in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When the main Wei army marched north, Taihong raided and captured the garrisons at Dongluo and Chukou, proclaiming that Liang reinforcements were close behind. The Di and Shu peoples rallied to him in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 太洪進圍關城，豎眼遣統軍姜喜等擊太洪，大破之，太洪棄關城走還。

translations.literal: Taihong advanced to besiege Guancheng. Shuyan sent the commanders Jiang Xi and others to attack Taihong and routed him severely. Taihong abandoned Guancheng and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Taihong advanced to besiege Guancheng. Shuyan sent Jiang Xi and other commanders against him and won a crushing victory. Taihong abandoned Guancheng and fled.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏以高陽王雍為太傅、領太尉，清河王懌為司徒，廣平王懷為司空。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Wei appointed Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong as Grand Tutor and concurrent Grand Commandant, Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi as Minister of Works, and Prince of Guangping Yuan Huai as Minister of Works in charge of public works.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the Northern Wei court appointed Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, grand tutor and concurrent grand commandant; Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, minister of works; and Yuan Huai, Prince of Guangping, minister in charge of public works.

sentences.zh: 甲午，魏葬宣武皇帝於景陵，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Wei buried Emperor Xuanwu at Jingling, with the temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, the Northern Wei court buried Emperor Xuanwu at Jingling, giving him the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 己亥，尊胡貴嬪為皇太妃。

translations.literal: On jihai, Honored Consort Hu was honored as imperial honored consort.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Honored Consort Hu was elevated to imperial honored consort.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲辰朔，以高太后為尼，徙居金墉瑤光寺，非大節慶，不得入宮。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the month (jiachen), Empress Dowager Gao was made a nun and moved to the Yaoguang Temple at Jinyong. Except on major festivals she was not permitted to enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the new moon, Empress Dowager Gao was forced to take the tonsure and was moved to the Yaoguang Temple at Jinyong. She was forbidden to enter the palace except on major festivals.

sentences.zh: 魏左僕射郭祚表稱：「蕭衍狂悖，謀斷川瀆，役苦民勞，危亡已兆；

translations.literal: Guo Zuo, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Wei, memorialized, saying, "Xiao Yan is arrogant and perverse. He plots to cut off the rivers and canals. The labor afflicts the people and toils them; the signs of peril and ruin are already visible;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo, left vice director of the Wei Secretariat, memorialized, "Xiao Yan is arrogant and reckless. He schemes to dam the rivers and canals, and his projects grind the people down with forced labor. The signs of ruin are already plain;

sentences.zh: 宜命將出師，長驅撲討。

translations.literal: it is fitting to command generals to take the field and drive forward in a long campaign to crush and punish him.
translations.idiomatic: we should send generals to take the field and drive deep into his territory to crush him.

sentences.zh: 」魏詔平南將軍楊大眼督諸軍鎮荊山。

translations.literal: " Wei issued an edict appointing the Pacifier of the South Yang Dayan to supervise all armies and garrison Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: " The Wei court ordered Yang Dayan, pacifier of the south, to supervise all armies and garrison Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 魏於忠既居門下，又總宿衛，遂專朝政，權傾一時。

translations.literal: Yu Zhong of Wei, having taken charge of the Secretariat and also commanding the palace guards, thereupon monopolized court government and his power tilted the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong of the Northern Wei court, having taken charge of the Secretariat and also commanding the palace guards, came to dominate the government, and his power eclipsed all others.

sentences.zh: 初，太和中，軍國多事，高祖以用度不足，百官之祿四分減一，忠悉命歸所減之祿。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era, with many military and state affairs, Emperor Gaozu, because expenditures were insufficient, had reduced all officials' salaries by one quarter. Zhong ordered all the reduced portions restored.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Taihe era, military and state demands were heavy and Emperor Xiaowen, finding revenue insufficient, had cut all officials' salaries by one quarter. Yu Zhong ordered the withheld portions restored in full.

sentences.zh: 舊制民稅絹一匹別輸綿八兩，布一區別輸麻十五斤，忠悉罷之。

translations.literal: Under the old system, for each bolt of silk cloth in the people's tax one paid an additional eight taels of floss, and for each piece of hemp cloth an additional fifteen catties of hemp. Zhong abolished all of these.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, for each bolt of silk in the people's tax an additional eight taels of floss had to be paid, and for each piece of hemp cloth an additional fifteen catties of hemp. Yu Zhong abolished all these surcharges.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔文武群官各進位一級。

translations.literal: On yichou, an edict advanced all civil and military officials one rank.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, an edict advanced every civil and military official one rank.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，浮山堰成而復潰。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, the Fushan dam was completed but then burst again.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Fushan dam was completed only to burst again.

sentences.zh: 或言蛟龍能乘風雨破堰，其性惡鐵；

translations.literal: Some said that flood dragons can ride wind and rain to break dams and that they hate iron;
translations.idiomatic: Some said flood dragons ride wind and rain to break dams and cannot abide iron;

sentences.zh: 乃運東、西冶鐵器數千萬斤沉之，亦不能合。

translations.literal: so they transported tens of millions of catties of ironware from the eastern and western foundries and sank them in the breach, yet still could not close it.
translations.idiomatic: so they sank tens of millions of catties of iron from the eastern and western foundries into the breach, yet still could not close it.

sentences.zh: 乃伐樹為井干，填以巨石；

translations.literal: They then felled trees to make cribwork and filled it with huge stones;
translations.idiomatic: They then felled trees to build cribwork and packed it with huge stones;

sentences.zh: 加土其上，緣淮百里內木石無鉅細皆盡，負簷者肩上皆穿，夏日疾疫，死者相枕，蠅蟲晝夜聲合。

translations.literal: piled earth on top. Within a hundred li along the Huai, timber and stone great and small were exhausted. Those who carried on shoulder poles had their shoulders worn through. In the summer heat plague spread; the dead lay pillow to pillow, and the sound of flies and insects merged day and night.
translations.idiomatic: and heaped earth on top. Within a hundred li along the Huai, every scrap of timber and stone was used up. Porters' shoulders were worn raw through their carrying poles. In the summer heat plague swept the works; the dead lay stacked upon one another, and the drone of flies and insects never ceased day or night.

sentences.zh: 魏梁州刺史薛懷吉破叛氐於沮水。

translations.literal: Xue Huaiji, Inspector of Liangzhou of Wei, defeated rebellious Di at Ju River.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huaiji, the Northern Wei inspector of Liangzhou, defeated rebellious Di forces at the Ju River.

sentences.zh: 懷吉，真度之子也。

translations.literal: Huaiji was a son of Zhendu.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiji was a son of Zhendu.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲寅，南秦州刺史崔暹又破叛氐，解武興之圍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiayin, Cui Xian, Inspector of Southern Qinzhou, again defeated rebellious Di and lifted the siege of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiayin, Cui Xian, inspector of Southern Qinzhou, again defeated rebellious Di forces and lifted the siege of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏冀州沙門法慶以妖幻惑眾，與勃海人李歸伯等作亂，推法慶為主。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the monk Fading of Jizhou in Wei deluded the masses with sorcery and illusion. With Li Guibo of Bohai and others he raised rebellion and made Fading their leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the monk Fading of Jizhou in the Northern Wei realm deluded the people with sorcery and, together with Li Guibo of Bohai and others, rose in rebellion and made Fading their leader.

sentences.zh: 法慶以尼惠暉為妻，以歸伯為十住菩薩、平魔軍司、定漢王，自號大乘。

translations.literal: Fading took the nun Huihui as his wife, made Guibo the Bodhisattva of the Ten Abodes, Pacifier of Demons Army Marshal, and King Who Settles Han, and styled himself Mahayana.
translations.idiomatic: Fading took the nun Huihui as his wife, appointed Guibo bodhisattva of the ten abodes, pacifier of demons and army marshal, and king who settles Han, and styled himself Mahayana.

sentences.zh: 又合狂藥，令人服之，父子兄弟不復相識，唯以殺害為事。

translations.literal: He also compounded a mad drug and made people take it, so that fathers and sons and brothers no longer recognized one another and cared only for killing.
translations.idiomatic: He also brewed a madness-inducing drug and forced people to take it, so that fathers, sons, and brothers no longer recognized one another and cared only for slaughter.

sentences.zh: 刺史蕭寶寅遣兼長史崔伯驎擊之，伯驎敗死。

translations.literal: The Inspector Xiao Baoyin sent the acting Chief Clerk Cui Boluo to attack them. Boluo was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xiao Baoyin sent his acting chief clerk Cui Boluo against them. Boluo was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 賊眾益盛，所在毀寺捨，斬僧尼，燒經像，云「新佛出世，除去眾魔。

translations.literal: The rebel host grew ever stronger. Wherever they went they destroyed temples and monasteries, beheaded monks and nuns, and burned sutras and images, saying, "A new Buddha has appeared in the world to remove all demons.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew ever stronger. Wherever they went they destroyed temples, beheaded monks and nuns, and burned sutras and images, proclaiming, "A new Buddha has come into the world to destroy all demons.

sentences.zh: 」秋，七月，丁未，詔假右光祿大夫元遙征北大將軍以討之。

translations.literal: " In autumn, in the seventh month, on dingwei, an edict provisionally appointed Yuan Yao, Right Honorary Grand Master of the Palace, as Grand General Who Conquers the North to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: " In autumn, in the seventh month, on dingwei, an edict provisionally appointed Yuan Yao, right honorary grand master of the palace, grand general who conquers the north, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書裴植，自謂人門不後王肅，以朝廷處之不高，意常怏怏，表請解官隱嵩山，世宗不許，深怪之。

translations.literal: Pei Zhi, Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Wei, considered that his family standing was not behind that of Wang Su. Because the court did not place him high enough, he was often discontented and memorialized requesting to resign office and retire to Mount Song. Emperor Shizong did not permit it and deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi, a director of the Wei Secretariat, believed his family standing was no less than Wang Su's. Because the court did not rank him highly enough, he was often discontented and asked to resign and retire to Mount Song. Emperor Xuanwu refused and came to resent him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及為尚書，志氣驕滿，每謂人曰：「非我須尚書，尚書亦須我。

translations.literal: When he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat, his spirit was proud and full. He often told people, "It is not that I need the Secretariat—the Secretariat also needs me.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became a director of the Secretariat, his pride swelled. He often told people, "It is not that I need the Secretariat—the Secretariat needs me.

sentences.zh: 」每入參議論，好面譏毀群官，又表徵南將軍田益宗，言：「華、夷異類，不應在百世衣冠之上。

translations.literal: " Whenever he entered to discuss policy he liked to mock and slander the officials to their faces. He also memorialized against the General Who Conquers the South Tian Yizong, saying, "Chinese and barbarians are different kinds and should not stand above the hundred generations of civilized families.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever he attended court to discuss policy, he delighted in mocking other officials to their faces. He also memorialized against Tian Yizong, general who conquers the south, saying, "Chinese and barbarians are different kinds and should not rank above families of long civilized standing.

sentences.zh: 」於忠、元昭見之切齒。

translations.literal: " Yu Zhong and Yuan Zhao gnashed their teeth at the sight of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Zhong and Yuan Zhao hated him for it with gnashing teeth.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射郭祚，冒進不已，自以東宮師傅，列辭尚書，望封侯、儀同，詔以祚為都督雍、岐、華三州諸軍事、征西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Guo Zuo, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, pressed forward without cease. Considering himself a tutor of the Eastern Palace, he repeatedly declined the Secretariat in hopes of a marquisate and the privilege of protocol equal to the Three Excellencies. An edict appointed Zuo Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yong, Qi, and Hua provinces, General Who Conquers the West, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo, left vice director of the Secretariat, ceaselessly pressed for advancement. As a former tutor of the Eastern Palace, he repeatedly tried to resign from the Secretariat in hopes of receiving a marquisate and protocol equal to the three excellencies. An edict appointed him commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Yong, Qi, and Hua provinces, general who conquers the west, and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 祚與植皆惡於忠專橫，密勸高陽王雍使出之；

translations.literal: Zuo and Zhi both hated Yu Zhong's monopoly and arrogance and secretly urged Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong to have him sent out of the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi both hated Yu Zhong's monopoly of power and secretly urged Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, to have him sent out of the capital;

sentences.zh: 忠聞之，大怒，令有司誣奏其罪。

translations.literal: Zhong heard of this, was greatly enraged, and ordered the authorities to fabricate charges and memorialize their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Zhong learned of this, he was furious and ordered the authorities to fabricate charges against them.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏：「羊祉告植姑子皇甫仲達云：『受植旨，詐稱被詔，帥合部曲欲圖於忠。

translations.literal: The Imperial Secretariat memorialized, "Yang Zhi reported that Zhi's nephew by marriage Huangfu Zhongda said, 'Receiving Zhi's instructions, I falsely claimed to have received an edict and would lead my followers to plot against Yu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat memorialized, "Yang Zhi reported that Pei Zhi's nephew by marriage Huangfu Zhongda said, 'On Pei Zhi's orders I falsely claimed to have received an edict and would lead my followers in a plot against Yu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 』臣等窮治，辭不伏引；

translations.literal: ' We exhausted the investigation, but he would not confess under interrogation;
translations.idiomatic: ' We investigated thoroughly, but he would not confess under interrogation;

sentences.zh: 然眾證明昺，准律當死。

translations.literal: yet the collective testimony is clear and bright, and by the law he should die.
translations.idiomatic: yet the collective testimony is clear, and by law he should die.

sentences.zh: 眾證雖不見植，皆言『仲達為植所使，植召仲達責問而不告列』。

translations.literal: Although the collective testimony does not directly implicate Zhi, all say, 'Zhongda was sent by Zhi; Zhi summoned Zhongda to question and reprove him but did not report him.'
translations.idiomatic: Although the collective testimony does not directly implicate Pei Zhi, all witnesses say, 'Zhongda acted on Pei Zhi's orders; Pei Zhi summoned Zhongda to question him but did not report him.'

sentences.zh: 推論情狀，不同之理不可分明，不得同之常獄，有所降減，計同仲達處植死刑。

translations.literal: Inferring the circumstances, the reasons for difference cannot be made clear, and it cannot be treated like an ordinary case with reduction of sentence. We calculate that Zhi should be sentenced to death like Zhongda.
translations.idiomatic: Inferring from the circumstances, the grounds for treating the cases differently cannot be made clear, and this cannot be handled like an ordinary case with a reduced sentence. We calculate that Pei Zhi should be sentenced to death like Zhongda.

sentences.zh: 植親帥城眾，附從王化，依律上議，乞賜裁處。

translations.literal: Zhi personally led the people of the city in submitting to royal transformation. According to the law we submit this for higher deliberation and beg that judgment be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi personally led the people of his city in submitting to the dynasty. According to law we submit this for higher deliberation and beg the throne to decide.

sentences.zh: 」忠矯詔曰：「凶謀既爾，罪不當恕；

translations.literal: " Zhong forged an edict saying, "Since the wicked plot is thus established, the crime may not be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Zhong forged an edict saying, "Since the wicked plot is established, the crime cannot be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 雖有歸化之誠，無容上議，亦不須待秋分。

translations.literal: although there was sincerity in submitting to transformation, there is no room for higher deliberation, nor need to wait for the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: although he showed sincerity in submitting to the dynasty, there is no room for higher deliberation, nor any need to wait for the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 」八月，己亥，植與郭祚及都水使者杜陵韋俊皆賜死。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month, on jihai, Zhi, Guo Zuo, and Wei Jun of Duling, Commissioner of Waterways, were all ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth month, on jihai, Pei Zhi, Guo Zuo, and Wei Jun of Duling, commissioner of waterways, were all ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 俊，祚之婚家也。

translations.literal: Jun was related to Zuo by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun was related to Guo Zuo by marriage.

sentences.zh: 忠又欲殺高陽王雍，崔光固執不從，乃免雍官，以王還第。

translations.literal: Zhong also wished to kill Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong. Cui Guang firmly refused to agree, so Yong was removed from office and sent back to his residence as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong also wanted to kill Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang. Cui Guang firmly refused to agree, so Yong was stripped of office and sent back to his princely residence.

sentences.zh: 朝野冤憤，莫不切齒。

translations.literal: Court and countryside were aggrieved at the injustice; all gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside seethed with outrage, and all gnashed their teeth in anger.

sentences.zh: 丙子，魏尊胡太妃為皇太后，居崇訓宮。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Wei honored Imperial Honored Consort Hu as empress dowager, with residence in the Palace of Honored Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the Northern Wei court elevated Imperial Honored Consort Hu to empress dowager, with residence in the Palace of Honored Instruction.

sentences.zh: 於忠領崇訓衛尉，劉騰為崇訓太僕，加侍中，侯剛為侍中撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Yu Zhong headed the Honored Instruction Guard Commandant, Liu Teng was Honored Instruction Grand Steward with the added title of palace attendant, and Hou Gang was palace attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong took charge as guard commandant of the Palace of Honored Instruction, Liu Teng became grand steward of the Palace of Honored Instruction with the added title of palace attendant, and Hou Gang was made palace attendant and general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 又以太后父國珍為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's father Guo Zhen was also made Honorary Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's father Guo Zhen was also appointed honorary grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，定州刺史田超秀帥眾三千降魏。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Tian Chaoxiu, Inspector of Dingzhou, led three thousand men in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Tian Chaoxiu, inspector of Dingzhou, led three thousand men in surrender to the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 戊子，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the Northern Wei court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏清河王懌進位太傅，領太尉，廣平王情為太保，領司徒，任城王澄為司空。

translations.literal: On jichou, Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi was advanced to Grand Tutor and concurrent Grand Commandant, Prince of Guangping Yuan Huai was made Grand Guardian and concurrent Minister of Works, and Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng was made Minister in charge of public works.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, was promoted to grand tutor and concurrent grand commandant; Yuan Huai, Prince of Guangping, was made grand guardian and concurrent minister of works; and Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, was made minister in charge of public works.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏以車騎大將軍於忠為尚書令，特進崔光為車騎大將軍，並加儀同三司。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Wei appointed Yu Zhong, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, as Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Cui Guang, Special Advanced, as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, both with the privilege of protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the Northern Wei court appointed Yu Zhong, grand general of chariots and cavalry, director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Cui Guang, special advanced, grand general of chariots and cavalry, both with protocol equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魏江陽王繼，熙之曾孫也，先為青州刺史，坐以良人為婢奪爵。

translations.literal: Yuan Ji, Prince of Jiangyang of Wei, was a great-grandson of Yuan Xi. He had earlier been Inspector of Qingzhou and was stripped of his title for taking a free commoner as a bondwoman.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ji, Prince of Jiangyang of the Northern Wei, was a great-grandson of Yuan Xi. He had earlier served as inspector of Qingzhou and was stripped of his title for taking a free commoner woman as a bondwoman.

sentences.zh: 繼子叉娶胡太后妹，壬辰，詔復繼本封，以叉為通直散騎侍郎，叉妻為新平郡君，仍拜女侍中。

translations.literal: Ji's son Cha married a younger sister of Empress Dowager Hu. On renchen, an edict restored Ji to his original fief, appointed Cha as Attendant Gentleman for Regular Service with the Imperial Equerry, made Cha's wife Lady of Xinping commandery, and also appointed her female palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Cha married a younger sister of Empress Dowager Hu. On renchen, an edict restored Ji to his original fief, appointed Cha attendant gentleman for regular service with the imperial equerry, made Cha's wife Lady of Xinping commandery, and also appointed her female palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 群臣奏請皇太后臨朝稱制，九月，乙未，靈太后始臨朝聽政，猶稱令以行事，群臣上書稱殿下。

translations.literal: The officials memorialized requesting that the empress dowager preside over court and hold the regency. In the ninth month, on yiwei, Empress Dowager Ling began to preside and hear government. She still issued orders to conduct affairs, and the officials in their memorials addressed her as "Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: The officials memorialized asking that the empress dowager preside over court and hold the regency. In the ninth month, on yiwei, Empress Dowager Ling began to preside and hear government. She still governed by edict, and officials in their memorials addressed her as "Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 太后聰悟，頗好讀書屬文，射能中針孔，政事皆手筆自決。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was intelligent and perceptive, quite fond of reading books and composing writing; in archery she could hit a needle's eye; in government affairs she decided everything herself by her own hand.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was quick-witted and perceptive, fond of reading and literary composition, and so skilled in archery that she could pierce a needle's eye; on all matters of government she decided by her own hand.

sentences.zh: 加胡國珍侍中，封安定公。

translations.literal: Hu Guozhen was added as palace attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guozhen was appointed palace attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 自郭祚等死，詔令生殺皆出於忠，王公畏之，重足脅息。

translations.literal: From the time Guo Zuo and the others died, edicts and orders over life and death all issued from Zhong; the princes and dukes feared him, standing on tiptoe and holding their breath.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Zuo and the others were put to death, every order of life or death issued from Yu Zhong; princes and high officials feared him and scarcely dared breathe.

sentences.zh: 太后既親政，乃解忠侍中、領軍、崇訓衛尉，止為儀同三司、尚書令。

translations.literal: Once the empress dowager had taken personal charge of government, she removed from Zhong his posts as palace attendant, commander of the palace guards, and guard commandant of the Palace of Honored Instruction, leaving him only with protocol equal to the three excellencies and director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress dowager assumed personal rule, she stripped Yu Zhong of his posts as palace attendant, commander of the palace guards, and guard commandant of the Palace of Honored Instruction, leaving him only protocol equal to the three excellencies and director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後旬餘，太后引門下侍官於崇訓宮，問曰：「忠在端揆，聲望何如？

translations.literal: More than ten days later, the empress dowager summoned the attendants of the Gate Department at the Palace of Honored Instruction and asked, "Zhong holds the chief minister's seat—what is his reputation like?
translations.idiomatic: A little over ten days later, the empress dowager summoned the attendants of the Gate Department at the Palace of Honored Instruction and asked, "Yu Zhong sits at the head of government—what is said of his reputation?

sentences.zh: 」鹹曰：「不稱闕任。

translations.literal: " All said, "He does not fit the vacancy of the post.
translations.idiomatic: " All replied, "He is not equal to the office."

sentences.zh: 」乃出忠為都督冀、定、瀛三州諸軍事、征北大將軍、冀州刺史；

translations.literal: " She then sent Zhong out as commander-in-chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Ji, Ding, and Ying, general who campaigns north, and inspector of Jizhou;
translations.idiomatic: " She then transferred Yu Zhong to serve as commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Ying, general who campaigns north, and inspector of Jizhou;

sentences.zh: 以司空澄領尚書令。

translations.literal: and she had the Minister in charge of public works Cheng take charge of the directorate of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and she had Yuan Cheng, minister in charge of public works, take charge as director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 澄奏：「安定公宜出入禁中，參咨大務。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "The Duke of Anding should enter and leave the inner palace and take part in consultation on great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "The Duke of Anding should be allowed to enter and leave the inner palace and take part in deliberation on major affairs.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，魏元遙破大乘賊，擒法慶並渠帥百餘人，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Yuan Yao of Wei defeated the Mahayana rebels, captured Fa Qing together with more than a hundred bandit chiefs, and sent their heads to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Yuan Yao of the Northern Wei defeated the Mahayana rebels, captured Fa Qing along with more than a hundred bandit chiefs, and sent their heads to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 左游擊將軍趙祖悅襲魏西硤石，據之以逼壽陽；

translations.literal: Left guerrilla general Zhao Zuyue raided Western Xishi of Wei, seized it, and used it to press Shouyang;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zuyue, left guerrilla general, raided Western Xishi in Wei territory, seized it, and used it to threaten Shouyang;

sentences.zh: 更築外城，徙緣淮之民以實城內。

translations.literal: he further built an outer wall and moved the people along the Huai to fill the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: he then built an outer wall and relocated people from along the Huai to populate the inner city.

sentences.zh: 將軍田道龍等散攻諸戍，魏揚州刺史李崇分遣諸將拒之。

translations.literal: Generals Tian Daolong and others scattered in attacks on the various garrisons; Li Chong, inspector of Yangzhou in Wei, sent out his generals in divisions to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Tian Daolong and others fanned out to attack the garrison posts; Li Chong, Northern Wei inspector of Yangzhou, dispatched his generals in separate columns to resist them.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，魏遣假鎮南將軍崔亮攻西硤石，又遣鎮東將軍蕭寶寅決淮堰。

translations.literal: On guihai, Wei sent acting general who pacifies the south Cui Liang to attack Western Xishi, and also sent general who pacifies the east Xiao Baoyin to breach the Huai dam.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the Northern Wei court sent acting general who pacifies the south Cui Liang to attack Western Xishi, and also sent general who pacifies the east Xiao Baoyin to breach the Huai dam.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙酉，魏以胡國珍為中書監、儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on yiyou, Wei appointed Hu Guozhen director of the Secretariat and protocol equal to the three excellencies, with his post as palace attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on yiyou, the Northern Wei court appointed Hu Guozhen director of the Secretariat with protocol equal to the three excellencies, while retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 甲午，弘化太守杜桂舉郡降魏。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Du Gui, administrator of Honghua, led the commandery in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Du Gui, administrator of Honghua, surrendered his commandery to the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，魏於忠用事，自言世宗許其優轉；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu Zhong held power in Wei, he said of himself that Emperor Shizong had promised him preferential advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Yu Zhong held power in the Northern Wei court, he claimed that Emperor Shizong had promised him preferential advancement;

sentences.zh: 太傅雍等皆不敢違，加忠車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yong and the others all dared not disobey, and Zhong was given the added title of grand general of chariots and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yuan Yong and the others all dared not refuse, and Yu Zhong was given the added title of grand general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 忠又自謂新故之際有定社稷之功，諷百僚令加己賞；

translations.literal: Zhong also considered that at the juncture between the new and the departed he had merit in stabilizing the altars of soil and grain, and he prompted the hundred officials to have rewards added for himself;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong also claimed that at the transition between emperors he had merit in securing the dynasty, and he prompted the officials to petition for his reward;

sentences.zh: 雍等議封忠常山郡公。

translations.literal: Yong and the others deliberated on enfeoffing Zhong as Duke of Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and the others agreed to enfeoff Yu Zhong as Duke of Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 忠又難於獨受，乃諷朝廷，同在門下者皆加封邑。

translations.literal: Zhong again found it difficult to accept alone, and so prompted the court that all who served together in the Gate Department should receive added fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong, unwilling to accept the honor alone, then prompted the court that all who had served with him in the Gate Department should receive added fiefs as well.

sentences.zh: 雍等不得已復封崔光為博平縣公，而尚書元昭等上訴不已。

translations.literal: Yong and the others, having no choice, again enfeoffed Cui Guang as Duke of Boxing county, but Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuan Zhao and others kept submitting appeals without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and the others, unable to refuse, also enfeoffed Cui Guang as Duke of Boxing county, but Yuan Zhao of the Secretariat and others kept submitting protests without cease.

sentences.zh: 太后敕公卿再議，太傅懌等上言：「先帝升遐，奉迎乘輿，侍衛省闥，乃臣子常職，不容以此為功。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered the dukes and ministers to deliberate again. Grand Tutor Yi and the others submitted, "When the late emperor ascended to the far journey, welcoming the imperial carriage and guarding the inner gates are the constant duties of subject and son—they cannot be taken as merit.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered the chief ministers to reconsider. Grand Tutor Yuan Yi and the others submitted, "When the late emperor passed away, welcoming the imperial carriage and guarding the inner gates were the ordinary duties of a subject—they cannot be counted as merit.

sentences.zh: 臣等前議授忠茅土，正以畏其威權，苟免暴戾故也。

translations.literal: We who earlier deliberated on granting Zhong a fief did so only because we feared his awesome power and wished to escape his violence.
translations.idiomatic: Our earlier deliberation to grant Yu Zhong a fief was made only out of fear of his power, to escape his violence.

sentences.zh: 若以功過相除，悉不應賞，請皆追奪。

translations.literal: If merit and fault are set against each other, none deserve reward; we request that all be revoked and seized back.
translations.idiomatic: If merit and fault are weighed together, none of us deserves reward; we ask that all honors be revoked.

sentences.zh: 」崔光亦奉送章綬茅土。

translations.literal: " Cui Guang also returned his seals, ribbons, and fief.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Guang also returned his seals, ribbons, and fief.

sentences.zh: 表十餘上，太后從之。

translations.literal: More than ten memorials were submitted, and the empress dowager approved.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten such memorials, the empress dowager approved.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍上表自劾，稱「臣初入柏堂，見詔旨之行一由門下，臣出君行，深知不可而不能禁；

translations.literal: Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, submitted a memorial impeaching himself, saying, "When I first entered the cypress hall, I saw that the execution of edicts was entirely through the Gate Department; the subject went out and the lord acted—I knew deeply that this was wrong but could not stop it;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, submitted a self-accusation, saying, "When I first entered the council chamber, I saw that every edict was issued through the Gate Department alone; though I knew this usurped the sovereign's authority, I could not stop it;

sentences.zh: 於忠專權，生殺自恣，而臣不能違。

translations.literal: Yu Zhong monopolized power and disposed of life and death at will, yet I could not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong wielded sole power and decided life and death as he pleased, yet I could not defy him.

sentences.zh: 忠規欲殺臣，賴在事執拒；

translations.literal: Zhong plotted to kill me, and I survived only because those on duty resisted;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong plotted to kill me, and I survived only because those on duty resisted on my behalf;

sentences.zh: 臣欲出忠於外，在心未行，返為忠廢。

translations.literal: I wished to send Zhong out to the provinces—the intent was in my heart but not carried out—and in return was dismissed by Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: I intended to transfer Yu Zhong to an outside post, but never acted on it, and was instead removed from office by him.

sentences.zh: 忝官尸祿，孤負恩私，請返私門，伏聽司敗。

translations.literal: I disgrace my office and consume salary in idleness, failing the grace shown me in private; I ask to return to my private home and submit to the judgment of the office of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I hold office unworthily, living on salary while betraying the emperor's grace; I ask to retire to my home and submit to whatever punishment the law requires.

sentences.zh: 」太后以忠有保護之功，不問其罪。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager, because Zhong had merit in protecting her, did not inquire into his crime.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager, crediting Yu Zhong with having protected her, did not pursue the matter against him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛丑，以雍為太師，領司州牧，尋復錄尚書事，與太傅懌、太保懷、侍中胡國珍入居門下，同厘庶政。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinchou, Yong was made Grand Preceptor and concurrent governor of Sizhou; soon he was again made recorder of the Imperial Secretariat, and together with Grand Tutor Yi, Grand Guardian Huai, and Palace Attendant Hu Guozhen he entered residence in the Gate Department and jointly managed the common affairs of government.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinchou, Yong was appointed grand preceptor and concurrent governor of Sizhou; soon he was restored as recorder of the Imperial Secretariat, and together with Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Grand Guardian Yuan Huai, and Palace Attendant Hu Guozhen he took up residence in the Gate Department to jointly manage affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏崔亮至硤石，趙祖悅逆戰而敗，閉城自守；

translations.literal: On jiyou, Cui Liang of Wei reached Xishi; Zhao Zuyue met him in battle and was defeated, shut the gates, and held himself inside;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Cui Liang of the Northern Wei reached Xishi; Zhao Zuyue met him in battle, was defeated, shut the gates, and held out within the city;

sentences.zh: 亮進圍之。

translations.literal: Liang advanced and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang pressed forward and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏主及太后謁景陵。

translations.literal: On yimao, the Wei sovereign and the empress dowager visited Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the Northern Wei emperor and the empress dowager visited Jingling.

sentences.zh: 是冬，寒甚，淮、泗盡凍，浮山堰士卒死者什七八。

translations.literal: That winter the cold was severe; the Huai and Si rivers froze solid, and seven or eight tenths of the soldiers at the Fushan dam died.
translations.idiomatic: That winter was bitterly cold; the Huai and Si rivers froze solid, and seven or eight tenths of the soldiers at the Fushan dam perished.

sentences.zh: 魏益州刺史傅豎眼，性清素，民、獠懷之。

translations.literal: Fu Shuyan, inspector of Yizhou in Wei, was by nature pure and plain, and the common people and indigenous tribes trusted in him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan, Northern Wei inspector of Yizhou, was honest and plain by nature, and the common people and indigenous tribes held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍元法僧代豎眼為益州刺史，素無治干，加以貪殘，王、賈諸姓，本州士族，法僧皆召為兵。

translations.literal: Longxiang General Yuan Faseng replaced Shuyan as inspector of Yizhou; he had never had governing ability, and to that was added greed and cruelty. The Wang, Jia, and other surnames, leading clans of the province—Faseng summoned them all as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Longxiang General Yuan Faseng replaced Fu Shuyan as inspector of Yizhou; he had no talent for governance and was moreover greedy and cruel. The Wang, Jia, and other leading clans of the province were all conscripted as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 葭萌民任令宗因眾心之患魏也，殺魏晉壽太守，以城來降，民、獠多應之；

translations.literal: Ren Lingzong of Jiameng, because the hearts of the people resented Wei, killed the Jinshou prefect of Wei and came with the city to surrender; many common people and indigenous tribes responded;
translations.idiomatic: Ren Lingzong of Jiameng, exploiting popular resentment of Wei rule, killed the Jinshou prefect and surrendered the city; many commoners and indigenous tribes joined him;

sentences.zh: 益州刺史鄱陽王恢遣巴西、梓潼二郡太守張齊將兵三萬迎之。

translations.literal: Prince of Poyang Hui, inspector of Yizhou, sent Zhang Qi, administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong, to lead thirty thousand troops to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Poyang Hui, inspector of Yizhou, sent Zhang Qi, administrator of Baxi and Zitong, with thirty thousand troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 法僧，熙之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Faseng was a great-grandson of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Faseng was a great-grandson of Yuan Xi.

sentences.zh: 魏岐州剌史趙王謐，干之子也，為政暴虐。

translations.literal: Zhao Mi, Prince of Zhao, inspector of Qizhou in Wei, was a son of Gan; his government was violent and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mi, Prince of Zhao and Northern Wei inspector of Qizhou, was a son of Yuan Gan; his rule was violent and cruel.

sentences.zh: 一旦，閉城門大索，執人而掠之，楚毒備至，又無故斬六人，闔城兇懼；

translations.literal: One day he shut the city gates and searched broadly, seizing people and plundering them; every torture was applied, and he also executed six men for no cause; the whole city was terrified;
translations.idiomatic: One day he shut the city gates and conducted a sweeping search, seizing people and plundering them with every torture imaginable; he also executed six men without cause, and terror seized the whole city;

sentences.zh: 眾遂大呼，屯門，謐登樓毀梯以自固。

translations.literal: the crowd then raised a great shout and massed at the gate; Mi climbed a tower, destroyed the stairs, and held himself secure.
translations.idiomatic: the people raised a great outcry and massed at the gates; Mi climbed a tower, destroyed the stairs, and barricaded himself inside.

sentences.zh: 胡太后遣游擊將軍王靖馳馹諭城人，城人開門謝罪，奉送管籥，乃罷謐剌史。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu sent guerrilla general Wang Jing on a relay horse to instruct the townspeople; the townspeople opened the gates, apologized, and presented the keys, and Mi was removed as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu sent guerrilla general Wang Jing posthaste to instruct the townspeople; they opened the gates, apologized, and surrendered the keys of the city, and Mi was removed from his post as inspector.

sentences.zh: 謐妃，太后從女也。

translations.literal: Mi's consort was the empress dowager's niece by a younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's consort was the empress dowager's niece.

sentences.zh: 至洛，除大司農卿。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang, he was appointed grand steward of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Luoyang, he was appointed grand steward of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 太后以魏主尚幼，未能親祭，欲代行祭事；

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because the Wei sovereign was still young and could not personally perform the sacrifices, wished to perform the sacrificial affairs in his stead;
translations.idiomatic: Because the Northern Wei emperor was still young and could not perform the sacrifices in person, the empress dowager wished to perform them on his behalf;

sentences.zh: 禮官博議，以為不可。

translations.literal: the ritual officials debated broadly and held that it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: the ritual officials debated at length and ruled that this was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 太后以問侍中崔光，光引漢和熹鄧太后祭宗廟故事，太后大悅，遂攝行祭事。

translations.literal: The empress dowager questioned Palace Attendant Cui Guang; Guang cited the precedent of Empress Dowager Deng of Han during the He and Xi reigns sacrificing at the ancestral temple; the empress dowager was greatly pleased and thereupon took charge of performing the sacrificial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager asked Palace Attendant Cui Guang; Guang cited the precedent of Empress Dowager Deng during the reigns of Emperors He and Xi sacrificing at the ancestral temple; the empress dowager was greatly pleased and took charge of the rites herself.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝四天監十五年（

translations.literal: The fifteenth year of Tianjian of Emperor Wu of Liang (
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianjian of Emperor Wu of Liang (

sentences.zh: 丙申，公元五一六年）

translations.literal: bingshen, corresponding to the year 516 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingshen, or 516 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊辰朔，魏大赦，改元熙平。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the first day of the month (wuchen), Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, the Northern Wei court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 魏崔亮攻硤石未下，與李崇屢約水陸並進，崇違期不至。

translations.literal: Cui Liang of Wei attacked Xishi but could not take it; he and Li Chong repeatedly agreed on simultaneous advance by land and water, but Chong failed to arrive by the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang of the Northern Wei besieged Xishi without success; he and Li Chong repeatedly agreed to advance together by land and water, but Li Chong failed to arrive on schedule.

sentences.zh: 胡太后以諸將不壹，乃以吏部尚書李平為使持節、鎮軍大將軍兼尚書右僕射，將步騎二千赴壽陽，別為行台，節度諸軍，如有乖異，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu, because the generals were not of one mind, appointed Li Ping, minister of personnel, as commissioner with full powers, general who pacifies the army and concurrent right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat, leading two thousand infantry and cavalry to Shouyang as a separate field headquarters to command all armies; where there was deviation, military law was to be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Because the generals were not united, Empress Dowager Hu appointed Li Ping, minister of personnel, commissioner with full powers, general who pacifies the army and concurrent right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat, and sent him with two thousand infantry and cavalry to Shouyang as a separate field headquarters to command all armies; any disobedience was to be punished by military law.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶寅遣輕車將軍劉智文等渡淮，攻破三壘；

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin sent Light Chariot General Liu Zhiwen and others across the Huai, broke three fortresses;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin sent Light Chariot General Liu Zhiwen and others across the Huai and captured three fortresses;

sentences.zh: 二月，乙巳，又敗將軍垣孟孫等於淮北。

translations.literal: in the second month, on yisi, he again defeated Generals Huan Mencun and others north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on yisi, he again defeated Generals Huan Mencun and others north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 李平至硤石，督李崇、崔亮等刻日水陸進攻，無敢乖互，戰屢有功。

translations.literal: Li Ping reached Xishi, supervised Li Chong, Cui Liang, and the others in setting a day for simultaneous attack by land and water; none dared to deviate, and in battle they repeatedly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping reached Xishi, set a fixed date for Li Chong, Cui Liang, and the others to attack together by land and water, and none dared disobey; they won repeated victories in battle.

sentences.zh: 上使左衛將軍昌義之將兵救浮山，未至，康絢已擊魏兵，卻之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Left Guard General Chang Yizhi to lead troops to rescue Fushan; before he arrived, Kang Xuan had already struck the Wei army and repulsed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor sent Left Guard General Chang Yizhi with troops to relieve Fushan; before he arrived, Kang Xuan had already attacked the Northern Wei army and driven it back.

sentences.zh: 上使義之與直閣王神念溯淮救硤石。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Yizhi and Direct Attendant Wang Shennian to go upstream on the Huai to rescue Xishi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chang Yizhi and Direct Attendant Wang Shennian to ascend the Huai and relieve Xishi.

sentences.zh: 崔亮遣將軍博陵崔延伯守下蔡，延伯與別將伊甕生夾淮為營。

translations.literal: Cui Liang sent General Boye Cui Yanbo to hold Xiaocai; Yanbo and another general Yi Wengsheng set camps on both banks of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang sent General Cui Yanbo of Boye to hold Xiaocai; Yanbo and another general, Yi Wengsheng, established camps on both banks of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 延伯取車輪去輞，削銳共輻，兩兩接對，揉竹為絲亙，貫連相屬，並十餘道，橫水為橋，兩頭施大鹿盧，出沒隨意，不可燒斫。

translations.literal: Yanbo took cart wheels, removed the rims, sharpened the hubs into points, paired them tip to tip, twisted bamboo into cord to span and link them—more than ten lanes in all—laid across the water as a bridge; at both ends he set up large capstans, so that they could appear and withdraw at will and could not be burned or chopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo took cart wheels, removed the rims, sharpened the hubs into points, paired them tip to tip, and bound them with twisted bamboo into more than ten floating lanes laid across the water as a bridge; large capstans at both ends let the structure be moved at will, and it could neither be burned nor cut apart.

sentences.zh: 既斷趙祖悅走路，又令戰艦不通，義之、神念屯梁城不得進。

translations.literal: Having cut off Zhao Zuyue's route of escape and also blocked the passage of warships, Yizhi and Shennian encamped at Liangcheng and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Having cut off Zhao Zuyue's escape route and blocked the passage of warships, Chang Yizhi and Wang Shennian encamped at Liangcheng and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 李平部分水陸攻硤石，克其外城；

translations.literal: Li Ping organized the land and water attack on Xishi and took its outer wall;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping organized a combined land and water assault on Xishi and captured the outer wall;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，祖悅出降，斬之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: on yichou, Zuyue came out and surrendered; he was executed, and his entire force was captured.
translations.idiomatic: on yichou, Zhao Zuyue came out and surrendered; he was executed, and his entire force was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 胡太后賜崔亮書，使乘勝深入。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu granted Cui Liang a letter ordering him to press the advantage and advance deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu sent Cui Liang a letter ordering him to press his advantage and advance in depth.

sentences.zh: 平部分諸將，水陸並進，攻浮山堰；

translations.literal: Ping organized the generals for simultaneous advance by land and water to attack the Fushan dam;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping organized the generals for a combined land and water advance against the Fushan dam;

sentences.zh: 亮違平節度，以疾請還，隨表輒發。

translations.literal: Liang disobeyed Ping's command, requested to return on grounds of illness, and as soon as his memorial was sent he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang disobeyed Li Ping's orders, requested leave on grounds of illness, and departed as soon as his memorial was dispatched.

sentences.zh: 平奏處亮死刑，太后令曰：「亮去留自擅，違我經略，雖有小捷，豈免大咎！

translations.literal: Ping memorialized requesting that Liang be sentenced to death; the empress dowager ordered, "Liang came and went at his own will, defying my strategy; though he had small victories, how can he escape great blame!
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping memorialized requesting the death penalty for Cui Liang; the empress dowager ordered, "Cui Liang came and went as he pleased, defying my strategy; though he won minor victories, how can he escape grave punishment!

sentences.zh: 但吾攝御萬機，庶幾惡殺，可特聽以功補過。

translations.literal: But I govern the ten thousand affairs and wish to avoid excessive killing; he may be specially allowed to offset fault with merit.
translations.idiomatic: But I govern ten thousand affairs and would rather not be excessive in killing; he may be specially permitted to offset his fault with his merit.

sentences.zh: 」魏師遂還。

translations.literal: " The Wei army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " The Northern Wei army then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏中尉元匡奏彈於忠：「幸國大災，專擅朝命，裴、郭受冤，宰輔黜辱。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang of Wei memorialized impeaching Yu Zhong: "Taking advantage of the state's great calamity, he monopolized court commands; Pei and Guo suffered false charges, and the chief ministers were humiliated and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang of the Northern Wei memorialized impeaching Yu Zhong: "Exploiting the state's great calamity, he monopolized court commands; Pei Zhi and Guo Zuo suffered false charges, and the chief ministers were humiliated and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 又自矯旨為儀同三司、尚書令，領崇訓衛尉，原其此意，欲以無上自處。

translations.literal: He also falsely altered edicts to make himself protocol equal to the three excellencies, director of the Imperial Secretariat, and head of the Honored Instruction guard; examining this intent, he wished to place himself above all authority.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged edicts appointing himself to protocol equal to the three excellencies, director of the Imperial Secretariat, and head of the Honored Instruction guard—clearly intending to set himself above all authority.

sentences.zh: 既事在恩後，宜加顯戮，請遣御史一人就州行決。

translations.literal: Since these matters occurred after the grace of pardon, he should receive conspicuous punishment; I request that one censor be sent to the province to carry out execution.
translations.idiomatic: Since these acts came after he had already received pardon, he deserves conspicuous punishment; I request that one censor be sent to his province to carry out the sentence.

sentences.zh: 自去歲世宗晏駕以後，皇太后未親覽以前，諸不由階級，或發門下詔書，或由中書宣敕，擅相拜授者，已經恩宥，正可免罪，並宜追奪。

translations.literal: From last year, after Emperor Shizong passed away and before the empress dowager personally attended to affairs, all who bypassed proper procedure—whether issuing edicts from the Gate Department or proclaimations from the Secretariat, or conferring appointments on their own—have already received grace and may be absolved of crime alone, but all such appointments should also be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Shizong's death last year, before the empress dowager assumed personal rule, all who bypassed proper channels—whether issuing Gate Department edicts, proclaiming Secretariat orders, or conferring appointments on their own—have already been pardoned and may be absolved of criminal liability, but all such appointments should likewise be revoked.

sentences.zh: 」太后令曰：「忠已蒙特原，無宜追罪；

translations.literal: " The empress dowager ordered, "Zhong has already received special pardon; there is no further ground to pursue punishment;
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager ordered, "Yu Zhong has already received special pardon; there is no further ground to pursue punishment;

sentences.zh: 餘如奏。

translations.literal: the rest as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder as submitted.

sentences.zh: 」匡又彈侍中侯剛掠殺羽林。

translations.literal: " Kuang also impeached Palace Attendant Hou Gang for seizing and killing guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Kuang also impeached Palace Attendant Hou Gang for seizing and killing guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 剛本以善烹調為嘗食典御，凡三十年，以有德於太后，頗專恣用事，王公皆畏附之。

translations.literal: Gang had originally been appointed food-taster for skill in cooking; for thirty years he served thus, and because he had shown virtue toward the empress dowager he acted with considerable arrogance in affairs; princes and dukes all feared him and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Gang had originally been appointed imperial food-taster for his skill in cooking; he served in that post for thirty years, and because he had done favors for the empress dowager he wielded considerable power; princes and high officials all feared him and sought his favor.

sentences.zh: 廷尉處剛大辟。

translations.literal: The court of justice sentenced Gang to execution.
translations.idiomatic: The court of justice sentenced Hou Gang to death.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「剛因公事掠人，邂逅致死，於律不坐。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "Gang seized a man on official business and killed him in the course of encounter; by law he is not liable.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Hou Gang seized a man in the course of official business and killed him in the heat of the moment; by law he is not liable.

sentences.zh: 」少卿陳郡袁翻曰：「『邂逅』，謂情狀已露，隱避不引，考訊以理者也。

translations.literal: " Vice Director Yuan Fan of Chen commandery said, "'Encounter' means that the circumstances are already exposed, one evades and will not confess, and questioning proceeds by reason.
translations.idiomatic: " Vice Director Yuan Fan of Chen commandery said, "'Encounter' applies when the facts are already exposed, the offender evades and will not confess, and questioning proceeds accordingly.

sentences.zh: 今此羽林，問則具首，剛口唱打殺，撾築非理，安得謂之『邂逅』！

translations.literal: In this case the guardsman, when questioned, confessed fully; Gang shouted to beat him to death and struck him unreasonably—how can this be called 'encounter'!
translations.idiomatic: But this guardsman confessed fully when questioned; Hou Gang shouted for him to be beaten to death and struck him without cause—how can this be called 'encounter'!

sentences.zh: 」太后乃削剛戶三百，解嘗食典御。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager then reduced Gang's household by three hundred and removed him as food-taster.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager then reduced Hou Gang's household by three hundred and removed him from his post as food-taster.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the month (wuxu), there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 魏論西硤石之功。

translations.literal: Wei deliberated on merit for the Western Xishi campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei court evaluated merit for the Western Xishi campaign.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以李崇為驃騎將軍，加儀同三司，李平為尚書右僕射，崔亮進號鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Li Chong was made Flying Cavalry General with added protocol equal to the three excellencies; Li Ping was made right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat; Cui Liang was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Li Chong was appointed flying cavalry general with protocol equal to the three excellencies; Li Ping was made right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat; and Cui Liang was promoted to general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 亮與平爭功於禁中，太后以亮為殿中尚書。

translations.literal: Liang and Ping contended for merit in the inner palace; the empress dowager made Liang director of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang and Li Ping contended for credit at court; the empress dowager appointed Liang director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 魏蕭寶寅在淮堰，上為手書誘之，使襲彭城，許送其國廟及室家諸比還北；

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin of Wei was at the Huai dam; the Emperor wrote him a letter in his own hand to entice him, urging him to raid Pengcheng and promising to send back his state temple tablets and his family and household when he returned north;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin of the Northern Wei was at the Huai dam; the Liang emperor wrote him a personal letter urging him to attack Pengcheng and promising to return his ancestral temple tablets, his family, and his household when he went back north;

sentences.zh: 寶寅表上其書於魏朝。

translations.literal: Baoyin submitted the letter to the Wei court.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin submitted the letter to the Northern Wei court.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，淮堰成，長九里，下廣一百四十丈，上廣四十五丈，高二十丈，樹以杞柳，軍壘列居其上。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, the Huai dam was completed: nine li long, one hundred forty zhang wide at the base, forty-five zhang wide at the top, twenty zhang high; it was planted with qi and willow, and military camps were arrayed upon it.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Huai dam was completed—nine li long, one hundred forty zhang wide at the base, forty-five zhang at the top, and twenty zhang high; qi and willow were planted on it, and military camps were built along its length.

sentences.zh: 或謂康絢曰：「四瀆，天所以節宣其氣，不可久塞，若鑿湫東注，則游波寬緩，堰得不壞。

translations.literal: Someone said to Kang Xuan, "The Four Rivers are Heaven's means to regulate and disperse its qi—they cannot be blocked for long; if the eastern outlet is opened, the flowing waves will spread gently and the dam will not be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Kang Xuan, "The Four Rivers are Heaven's way of regulating and dispersing its forces—they cannot be dammed forever; if the eastern outlet is opened, the water will spread gently and the dam will hold.

sentences.zh: 」絢乃開湫東注。

translations.literal: " Xuan then opened the eastern outlet.
translations.idiomatic: " Kang Xuan then opened the eastern outlet.

sentences.zh: 又縱反間於魏曰：「梁人所懼開湫，不畏野戰。

translations.literal: He also spread counter-intelligence toward Wei, saying, "The Liang people fear the opening of the outlet; they do not fear field battle.
translations.idiomatic: He also spread disinformation to the Northern Wei, saying, "The Liang forces fear the opening of the outlet; they do not fear field battle.

sentences.zh: 」蕭寶寅信之，鑿山深五丈，開湫北注，水日夜分流猶不減，魏軍竟罷歸。

translations.literal: " Xiao Baoyin believed this, dug into the mountain five zhang deep, and opened the northern outlet; water split day and night yet still did not diminish, and the Wei army finally abandoned the effort and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Baoyin believed it, dug five zhang into the mountain, and opened the northern outlet; water flowed out day and night yet the level did not fall, and the Northern Wei army finally gave up and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 水之所及，夾淮方數百里。

translations.literal: Where the water reached, on both banks of the Huai for several hundred li,
translations.idiomatic: The flood spread for several hundred li along both banks of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 李崇作浮橋於硤石戍間，又築魏昌城於八公山東南，以備壽陽城壞。

translations.literal: Li Chong built a floating bridge between the Xishi garrison and also fortified Weichang city southeast of Bagong Mountain, to guard against the walls of Shouyang collapsing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong built a floating bridge near the Xishi garrison and also fortified Weichang city southeast of Bagong Mountain, as a precaution against Shouyang's walls being undermined.

sentences.zh: 居民散就岡壟，其水清澈，俯視廬舍塚墓，了然在下。

translations.literal: The people scattered and took refuge on mounds and ridges; the water was clear, and looking down, dwellings, tombs, and graves lay plainly visible below.
translations.idiomatic: The people fled to the hillocks and ridges; the floodwaters ran clear, and from above one could look straight down at houses and graves laid bare beneath the surface.

sentences.zh: 初，堰起於徐州境內，刺史張豹子宣言，謂己必掌其事；

translations.literal: At first the dam was raised within the borders of Xuzhou; the inspector Zhang Baozi proclaimed publicly that he himself would surely oversee the work;
translations.idiomatic: When work on the dam began within Xuzhou, Inspector Zhang Baozi declared openly that he would surely be put in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 既而康絢以他官來監作，豹子甚慚。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Kang Xuan came as supervisor of construction in another capacity, and Baozi was deeply ashamed.
