translations.idiomatic: Before long, however, Kang Xuan arrived in another official capacity to supervise the project, and Baozi was deeply mortified.

sentences.zh: 俄而敕豹子受絢節度，豹子遂譖絢與魏交通，上雖不納，猶以事畢征絢還。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Baozi to accept Xuan's command; Baozi then slandered Xuan, saying he had dealings with Wei; though the emperor did not accept this, he still recalled Xuan once the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon followed ordering Baozi to serve under Kang Xuan's command. Baozi then accused Xuan of colluding with Wei. The emperor did not believe him, but once the work was done he nevertheless recalled Xuan.

sentences.zh: 魏胡太后追思於忠之功，曰：「豈宜以一謬棄其餘勳！

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu of Wei, recalling Yu Zhong's merits, said: "How can one error be allowed to cancel out all his other achievements!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu of Wei, thinking back on Yu Zhong's service, said, "How can a single fault wipe away all his other merits!

sentences.zh: 」復封忠為靈壽縣公，亦封崔光為平恩縣侯。

translations.literal: " She again enfeoffed Zhong as Duke of Lingshou County and also enfeoffed Cui Guang as Marquis of Ping'en County.
translations.idiomatic: " She restored Zhong as Duke of Lingshou County and also enfeoffed Cui Guang as Marquis of Ping'en County.

sentences.zh: 魏元法僧遣其子景隆將兵拒張齊，齊與戰於葭萌，大破之，屠十餘者，遂圍武興。

translations.literal: Yuan Faseng of Wei sent his son Jinglong to lead troops against Zhang Qi; Qi fought him at Jiameng, routed him utterly, slaughtered ten-odd [foes], and then besieged Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Faseng of Wei sent his son Jinglong with an army to oppose Zhang Qi. Qi met him at Jiameng, crushed his forces, slaughtered more than ten strongholds, and then laid siege to Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 法僧嬰城自守，境內皆叛，法僧遣使間道告急於魏。

translations.literal: Faseng held the city and defended himself; the whole region within his borders rebelled, and Faseng sent envoys by hidden routes to Wei to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Faseng shut himself within the city to hold out, while the whole region rose against him. He sent messengers by secret paths to Wei to plead for help.

sentences.zh: 魏驛召鎮南軍司傅豎眼於淮南，以為益州刺史、西征都督，將步騎三千以赴之。

translations.literal: Wei dispatched a courier to summon Fu Shuyan, army commander of the southern garrison, from Huainan, appointing him inspector of Yizhou and commander-in-chief of the western expedition, and sent three thousand infantry and cavalry to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent a fast courier to summon Fu Shuyan, the southern garrison army commander, from Huainan, made him inspector of Yizhou and commander-in-chief of the western expedition, and sent three thousand foot and horse to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 豎眼入境，轉戰三日，行二百餘里，九遇皆捷。

translations.literal: Shuyan entered the territory, fought continuously for three days, marched more than two hundred li, and won victory in nine encounters.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan crossed the border and fought without pause for three days, advancing more than two hundred li and winning every one of nine engagements.

sentences.zh: 五月，豎眼擊殺梁州刺史任太洪。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Shuyan struck down and killed Liang Inspector Ren Taihong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Shuyan killed Liang Inspector Ren Taihong in battle.

sentences.zh: 民、獠聞豎眼至，皆喜，迎拜於路者相繼。

translations.literal: When the people and the Liao tribes heard that Shuyan had arrived, all rejoiced, and those who welcomed and bowed to him along the road followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When the common people and the Liao tribes learned that Shuyan had come, they rejoiced, and people lined the roads to welcome and salute him.

sentences.zh: 張齊退保白水，豎眼入州，白水以東民皆安業。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi withdrew to defend Baishui; Shuyan entered the province, and east of Baishui the people all returned to their occupations in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi fell back to Baishui. Shuyan entered the province, and east of Baishui the people settled back into their lives.

sentences.zh: 魏梓潼太守苟金龍領關城戍主，梁兵至，金龍疾病，不堪部分，其妻劉氏帥厲城民，乘城拒戰，百有餘日，士卒死傷過半。

translations.literal: Gou Jinlong, Wei prefect of Zitong, also served as garrison commander of Guancheng; when Liang troops arrived, Jinlong was ill and could not command; his wife, Lady Liu, rallied and encouraged the townspeople, mounted the walls, and resisted battle for more than a hundred days, until more than half the soldiers were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Jinlong, Wei prefect of Zitong and commander of the Guancheng garrison, fell gravely ill when Liang forces arrived and could no longer direct the defense. His wife, Lady Liu, rallied the townspeople, manned the walls, and held out for more than a hundred days, until casualties exceeded half the garrison.

sentences.zh: 戍副高景謀叛，劉氏斬景及其黨與數千人，自餘將士，分衣減食，勞逸必同，莫不畏而懷之。

translations.literal: The deputy garrison commander Gao Jing plotted rebellion; Lady Liu executed Jing and several thousand of his accomplices; as for the remaining officers and soldiers, she shared out clothing and reduced rations, sharing hardship and ease alike, so that none failed to fear her and yet all cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Gao Jing plotted treason. Lady Liu executed him and several thousand of his followers. She then divided clothing and cut rations among the remaining troops, sharing every hardship and comfort with them, until all feared her and yet all revered her.

sentences.zh: 井在城外，為梁兵所據。

translations.literal: The wells were outside the city and had been seized by Liang troops.
translations.idiomatic: The wells lay outside the walls and were held by the Liang army.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，劉氏命出公私布絹及衣服懸之，絞而取水，城中所有雜物悉儲之。

translations.literal: It happened that heaven sent heavy rain; Lady Liu ordered public and private cloth, silk, and garments brought out and hung up, wrung them to obtain water, and stored every sort of thing in the city.
translations.idiomatic: Then came a great rain. Lady Liu had public and private cloth, silk, and clothing hung out, wrung them for water, and stored every scrap of material in the city that might hold moisture.

sentences.zh: 豎眼至，梁兵乃退，魏人封其子為平昌縣子。

translations.literal: When Shuyan arrived, the Liang troops withdrew; the people of Wei enfeoffed her son as Viscount of Pingchang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Shuyan arrived, the Liang army withdrew. Wei enfeoffed her son as Viscount of Pingchang County.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚子，以尚書令王瑩為左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，尚書右僕射袁昂為左僕射，吏部尚書王暕為右樸射。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Wang Ying, director of the Secretariat, was made Left Grand Master of the Palace and given the rank of Opening the Office with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies; Yuan Ang, right vice director of the Secretariat, was made Left Vice Director; Wang Yan, director of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Wang Ying, director of the Secretariat, was appointed Left Grand Master of the Palace with the rank of Opening the Office with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies; Yuan Ang, right vice director of the Secretariat, became Left Vice Director; and Wang Yan, director of the Ministry of Personnel, became Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 暕，儉之子也。

translations.literal: Yan was the son of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was the son of Jian.

sentences.zh: 張齊數出白水侵魏葭萌，傅豎眼遣虎威將軍強虯攻信義將軍楊興起，殺之，復取白水。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi repeatedly sallied from Baishui to raid Wei's Jiameng; Fu Shuyan sent Tiger Might General Qiang Qiu to attack Faithful Integrity General Yang Xingqi, killed him, and recovered Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi repeatedly raided Wei's Jiameng from Baishui. Fu Shuyan sent Tiger Might General Qiang Qiu against Faithful Integrity General Yang Xingqi, killed him, and retook Baishui.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍王光昭又敗於陽平，張齊親帥驍勇二萬餘人與傅豎眼戰。

translations.literal: Pacifying the North General Wang Guangzhao was again defeated at Yangping; Zhang Qi personally led more than twenty thousand picked warriors to fight Fu Shuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the North General Wang Guangzhao was defeated again at Yangping. Zhang Qi then personally led more than twenty thousand elite troops against Fu Shuyan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，齊軍大敗，走還，小劍、大劍諸戍皆棄城走，東益州復入於魏。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Qi's army was utterly defeated and fled back; the garrisons at Xiaojian, Dajian, and elsewhere all abandoned their cities and fled, and Eastern Yizhou was restored to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Qi's army was routed and driven back. The garrisons at Xiaojian, Dajian, and elsewhere were abandoned, and Eastern Yizhou returned to Wei.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙巳，魏以胡國珍為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yisi, Wei appointed Hu Guozhen Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with the rank of Opening the Office with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yisi, Wei made Hu Guozhen Grand General of Agile Cavalry with the rank of Opening the Office with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies and appointed him inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 國珍年老，太后實不欲令出，止欲示以方面之榮；

translations.literal: Guozhen was old in years; the empress dowager in truth did not wish to send him out, but only meant to display to him the honor of a frontier command;
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was advanced in years. The empress dowager had no real intention of sending him out; she meant only to bestow on him the honor of a regional command.

sentences.zh: 竟不行。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 康絢既還，張豹子不復修淮堰。

translations.literal: After Kang Xuan had returned, Zhang Baozi no longer repaired the Huai dam.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kang Xuan had been recalled, Zhang Baozi ceased repairing the Huai dam.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁丑，淮水暴漲，堰壞，其聲如雷，聞三百里，緣淮城戍村落十餘萬口皆漂入海。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingchou, the Huai River rose violently, the dam broke, the sound was like thunder and could be heard for three hundred li, and more than a hundred thousand people in cities, garrisons, and villages along the Huai were swept into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingchou, the Huai surged and the dam collapsed with a thunderous roar heard three hundred li away. More than a hundred thousand people in towns, garrisons, and villages along the river were swept out to sea.

sentences.zh: 初，魏人患淮堰，以任城王澄為大將軍、大都督南討諸軍事，勒眾十萬，將出徐州來攻堰；

translations.literal: Earlier, the people of Wei had been troubled by the Huai dam and appointed Prince Cheng of Rencheng grand general and commander-in-chief of all armies for the southern punitive campaign, mustering a hundred thousand men and preparing to march out from Xuzhou to attack the dam;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, troubled by the Huai dam, Wei had appointed Prince Cheng of Rencheng grand general and commander-in-chief of the southern campaign, mustered a hundred thousand men, and prepared to march from Xuzhou to destroy it.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射李平以為：「不假兵力，終當自壞。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Ping said: "Without borrowing military force, it will in the end collapse of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Li Ping argued, "There is no need for troops. In time it will destroy itself.

sentences.zh: 」及聞破，太后大喜，賞平甚厚，澄遂不行。

translations.literal: " When word came that it had broken, the empress dowager was greatly pleased, rewarded Ping very generously, and Cheng then did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When news came that the dam had broken, the empress dowager was overjoyed, rewarded Ping lavishly, and Cheng's expedition was canceled.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，大赦。

translations.literal: On renchen, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 魏胡太后數幸宗戚勳貴之家，侍中崔光表諫曰：「《禮》，諸侯非問疾弔喪而入諸臣之家，謂之君臣為謔。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu of Wei repeatedly visited the homes of imperial kin and meritorious nobles; Palace Attendant Cui Guang submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "According to the Rites, when a feudal lord enters his ministers' homes for any purpose other than inquiring after illness or mourning the dead, it is called ruler and subject making sport together.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu of Wei often visited the homes of imperial clansmen and meritorious nobles. Palace Attendant Cui Guang remonstrated in a memorial: "The Rites say that when a feudal lord enters a minister's house for any reason other than to inquire after illness or offer condolences, it is called ruler and subject treating one another as playthings.

sentences.zh: 不言王后夫人，明無適臣家之義。

translations.literal: It does not speak of queens and consorts, making clear that there is no propriety in going to ministers' homes.
translations.idiomatic: The text does not mention queens and consorts, making plain that there is no proper occasion for them to visit ministers' houses.

sentences.zh: 夫人，父母在有歸寧，沒則使卿寧。

translations.literal: As for a lady, while her parents are alive she may return home for a visit; after they die, she sends a minister to inquire after her family.
translations.idiomatic: A lady may return to her parents' home while they live; after their death she sends an envoy to inquire after her family.

sentences.zh: 漢上官皇后將廢昌邑，霍光，外祖也，親為宰輔，後猶御武帳以接群臣，示男女之別也。

translations.literal: In Han, when Empress Shangguan was about to depose the King of Changyi, Huo Guang—her maternal grandfather—though he personally served as chief minister, the empress still received the ministers from behind a military screen to show the separation between male and female.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, when Empress Shangguan was about to depose the King of Changyi, Huo Guang—her maternal grandfather and chief minister—still received the ministers from behind a military screen, preserving the distinction between the sexes.

sentences.zh: 今帝族方衍，勳貴增遷，祗請遂多，將成彝式。

translations.literal: Now the imperial clan is expanding, meritorious nobles are rising in rank one after another, and respectful invitations are multiplying, until this is becoming established custom.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial clan grows ever larger, meritorious nobles rise in rank without cease, and invitations multiply until they threaten to become fixed custom.

sentences.zh: 願陛下簡息游幸，則率土屬賴，含生仰悅矣。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will reduce and cease these pleasure visits; then all within the realm will depend on you, and every living being will look up in joy.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to curtail these pleasure visits. Then the whole realm will look to you in trust, and all living things will rejoice.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄以北邊鎮將選舉彌輕，恐賊虜窺邊，山陵危迫，奏求重鎮將之選，修警備之嚴，詔公卿議之。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng, because selection for northern frontier garrison commanders was growing ever laxer, feared that bandits and barbarians would spy on the border and that the imperial tombs would be placed in peril, memorialized asking that the choice of frontier commanders be made weightier and border defenses strengthened; an edict ordered the high ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng, alarmed that appointments to the northern frontier garrisons were growing ever more careless and fearing that enemies might probe the border and threaten the imperial tombs, asked that frontier commanders be chosen with greater rigor and defenses tightened. The court ordered the high ministers to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 廷尉少卿袁翻議，以為：「比緣邊州郡官不擇人，唯論資級。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Fan argued, saying: "Recently, because frontier prefectures and districts do not choose men for their merit but judge only by rank and seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Fan argued: "Of late, frontier prefectures and districts have not chosen men for ability but have looked only to rank and seniority.

sentences.zh: 或值貪污之人，廣開戍邏，多置帥領；

translations.literal: Sometimes one encounters corrupt men, who broadly open garrison posts and multiply commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes corrupt officials are appointed, who multiply garrison posts and stack on commanders;

sentences.zh: 或用其左右姻親；

translations.literal: Sometimes they employ their close associates and in-laws;
translations.idiomatic: sometimes they install their own retainers and in-laws;

sentences.zh: 或受人貨財請屬。

translations.literal: Sometimes they accept bribes and private requests for appointments.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes they take bribes and grant posts through favor.

sentences.zh: 皆無防寇之心，唯有聚斂之意。

translations.literal: All alike lack any mind to guard against invaders and harbor only the intent to amass wealth.
translations.idiomatic: None of them think of defending the frontier; all they want is to enrich themselves.

sentences.zh: 其勇力之兵，驅令抄掠，若值強敵，即為奴虜，如有執獲，奪為己富。

translations.literal: As for the strong and brave soldiers, they are driven to raid and plunder; if they meet a powerful foe they become slaves and captives, and if they take anything they seize it for their own wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The strong soldiers are sent out to raid. When they meet a powerful enemy they are taken captive; when they capture anything they keep it for themselves.

sentences.zh: 其羸弱老小之輩，微解金鐵之工，少閒草木之作，無不搜營窮壘，苦役百端。

translations.literal: As for the weak, the old, and the young, those who know even a little of metal and iron work or a bit of work with plants and trees—all are hunted out from every camp and stronghold and put to bitter labor in every form.
translations.idiomatic: The weak, the old, and the young—anyone who knows even a little metalwork or a bit of farming—is dragged from every camp and fortress and put to every sort of cruel labor.

sentences.zh: 自餘或伐木深山，或芸草平陸，販貿往還，相望道路。

translations.literal: The rest may cut timber in deep mountains, weed grass on level ground, or go back and forth in trade, filling the roads as far as the eye can see.
translations.idiomatic: Others cut timber in deep mountains, weed fields on the plains, or travel the roads in endless trade.

sentences.zh: 此等祿既不多，貲亦有限，皆收其實絹，給其虛粟，窮其力，薄其衣，用其功，節其食，綿冬歷夏，加方疾苦，死於溝瀆者什常七八。

translations.literal: For such men, salaries are already not great and possessions are also limited; yet all their real silk is taken from them while empty grain is given in return; their strength is exhausted, their clothing is thin, their labor is used, their food is rationed; through winter into summer, with added hardship and illness, seven or eight out of ten die in ditches and drains.
translations.idiomatic: Their pay is meager and their goods few, yet commanders take their real silk and pay them in worthless grain. They are worked to exhaustion, clothed in rags, fed on scraps, and driven without rest from winter through summer, until added hardship and disease kill seven or eight out of ten in ditches and drains.

sentences.zh: 是以鄰敵伺間，擾我疆場，皆由邊任不得其人故也。

translations.literal: Therefore neighboring enemies watch for openings and harass our borders—all because frontier appointments do not obtain the right men.
translations.idiomatic: That is why neighboring enemies watch for openings and raid our borders: the wrong men hold the frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 愚謂自今已後，南北邊諸籓及所統郡縣府佐、統軍至於戍主，皆令朝臣王公已下各舉所知，必選其才，不拘階級；

translations.literal: I humbly propose that from now on, for all frontier principalities north and south and for the assistants in the prefectures, districts, and offices under them, from army commanders down to garrison chiefs, court ministers, princes, and officials below them should each recommend men they know, choosing talent without regard to rank;
translations.idiomatic: I propose that henceforth, for every frontier domain north and south and for all their prefectural, district, and staff appointments, from army commanders down to garrison chiefs, every court minister and prince should recommend men known to him, choosing talent without regard to rank.

sentences.zh: 若稱職及敗官，並所舉之人隨事賞罰。

translations.literal: If the appointee proves competent or fails in office, the recommender too should be rewarded or punished according to the case.
translations.idiomatic: If an appointee succeeds or fails, the man who recommended him should be rewarded or punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」太后不能用。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager could not adopt this.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 及正光之末，北邊盜賊群起，遂逼舊都，犯山陵，如澄所慮。

translations.literal: By the end of the Zhengguang era, bandits rose in groups on the northern frontier, pressed upon the old capital, and violated the imperial tombs, just as Cheng had feared.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhengguang era, bandits rose all along the northern frontier, threatened the old capital, and violated the imperial tombs—just as Cheng had warned.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，交州刺史李畟斬交州反者阮宗孝，傳首建康。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Li Bi, inspector of Jiaozhou, executed the Jiaozhou rebel Ruan Zongxiao and sent his head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, Li Bi, inspector of Jiaozhou, executed the rebel Ruan Zongxiao and sent his head to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 初，魏世宗作瑤光寺，未就，是歲，胡太后又作永寧寺，皆在宮側；

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Shizong of Wei had begun Yaoguang Temple, but it was not yet finished; that year, Empress Dowager Hu also built Yongning Temple; both stood beside the palace;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Shizong of Wei had begun Yaoguang Temple but left it unfinished. That year Empress Dowager Hu also built Yongning Temple. Both stood beside the palace.

sentences.zh: 又作石窟寺於伊闕口，皆極土木之美。

translations.literal: She also built Shiku Temple at the Yique Pass, all of them reaching the utmost in the beauty of timber and earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: She also built Shiku Temple at the Yique Pass. All were monuments to the most lavish architecture.

sentences.zh: 而永寧尤盛，有金像高丈八尺者一，如中人者十，玉像二。

translations.literal: Yet Yongning was especially magnificent: one gold image eighteen feet high, ten like a man of middling height, and two jade images.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning surpassed them all. It held one gold image eighteen feet high, ten the size of a man, and two of jade.

sentences.zh: 為九層浮圖，掘地築基，下及黃泉；

translations.literal: She built a nine-story pagoda, digging earth and laying foundations down to the Yellow Springs;
translations.idiomatic: Its nine-story pagoda was dug deep into the earth, its foundations reaching to the Yellow Springs.

sentences.zh: 浮圖高九十丈，上剎得高十丈，每夜靜，鈴鐸聲聞十里。

translations.literal: The pagoda stood ninety zhang high, and the finial atop it added another ten zhang; each quiet night, the bells and chimes could be heard ten li away.
translations.idiomatic: The pagoda rose ninety zhang, its spire another ten. On quiet nights the bells and chimes could be heard ten li away.

sentences.zh: 佛殿如太極殿，南門如端門。

translations.literal: The Buddha hall was like the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and the south gate like the Gate of Duan.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha hall rivaled the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the south gate rivaled the Gate of Duan.

sentences.zh: 僧房千間，珠玉錦繡，駭人心目。

translations.literal: There were a thousand monks' quarters, with pearls, jade, brocade, and embroidery that stunned the eye.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand monks' quarters blazed with pearls, jade, brocade, and embroidery that dazzled the eye.

sentences.zh: 自佛法入中國，塔廟之盛，未之有也。

translations.literal: Since the Buddha's teaching entered China, there had never been such magnificence in pagodas and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Buddha's teaching came to China, no temple or pagoda had ever been so grand.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史李崇上表，以為：「高祖遷都垂三十年，明堂未修，太學荒廢，城闕府寺頗亦頹壞，非所以追隆堂構，儀刑萬國者也。

translations.literal: Li Chong, inspector of Yangzhou, submitted a memorial, saying: "It has been nearly thirty years since Emperor Gaozu moved the capital; the Bright Hall has not been repaired, the Imperial Academy lies abandoned, and the city gates and government temples are also much decayed—this is not the way to pursue the exaltation of the royal hall and serve as a model for the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, inspector of Yangzhou, memorialized: "Nearly thirty years have passed since Emperor Gaozu moved the capital, yet the Bright Hall remains unrepaired, the Imperial Academy lies in ruins, and the city gates and government halls are crumbling. This is no way to honor the founding of the dynasty or set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 今國子雖有學官之名，而無教授之實，何異兔絲、燕麥，南箕、北斗！

translations.literal: Now the Directorate of Education, though it bears the name of a school office, has none of the reality of instruction—how is this different from dodder and wild oats, or the Winnowing Basket and the Northern Dipper!
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Education bears the name of a school but does no teaching—no more real than dodder pretending to be grain, or the Winnowing Basket mistaken for the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 事不兩興，須有進退；

translations.literal: Two great undertakings cannot rise together; one must choose advance or retreat;
translations.idiomatic: Great works cannot all be pursued at once. One must choose.

sentences.zh: 宜罷尚方雕靡之作，省永寧土木之功，減瑤光材瓦之力，分石窟鐫琢之勞，及諸事役非急者，於三時農隙修此數條，使國容嚴顯，禮化興行，不亦休哉！

translations.literal: It would be fitting to cease the ornate works of the Palace Workshops, reduce the timber-and-earth labor on Yongning, cut back the materials and tiles for Yaoguang, divide the carving labor at Shiku, and together with other non-urgent corvée tasks, repair these several items in the agricultural off-seasons of the three seasons, so that the state's dignity may stand forth in majesty and ritual and transformation flourish—would this not be excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Stop the Palace Workshops' ornamental projects. Cut back construction at Yongning, reduce materials for Yaoguang, divert labor from the stone carvings at Shiku, and suspend every non-urgent public work. Use the farming seasons' intervals to repair the Bright Hall, the Academy, and the capital's halls and gates. Then the state's dignity would stand forth and ritual civilization would flourish. Would that not be glorious?

sentences.zh: 」太后優令答之，而不用其言。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager replied with a gracious edict, but did not adopt his words.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager answered with a gracious edict, but ignored his advice.

sentences.zh: 太后好事佛，民多絕戶為沙門，高陽王友李瑒上言：「三千之罪莫大於不孝，不孝之大無過於絕祀。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was devoted to Buddhism; many among the people broke off their households to become monks. Li Yang, a friend to the Prince of Gaoyang, submitted a memorial, saying: "Among the three thousand offenses, none is greater than unfilial conduct, and among unfilial acts none surpasses cutting off the ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was devoted to Buddhism, and many people abandoned their households to become monks. Li Yang, a friend to the Prince of Gaoyang, memorialized: "Of the three thousand offenses, none is greater than unfilial conduct, and of unfilial acts none is worse than ending the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 豈得輕縱背禮之情，肆其向法之意，一身親老，棄家絕養，缺當世之禮而求將來之益！

translations.literal: How can one lightly indulge the feeling of turning against ritual, give free rein to the intent of turning toward the Law, leave parents in old age, abandon home and cut off support, neglect the rites of this life and seek benefit in the life to come!
translations.idiomatic: How can we lightly indulge those who turn against ritual and rush toward the Law—who leave aging parents, abandon home and cut off support, neglect the duties of this life, and chase after rewards in the next!

sentences.zh: 孔子云：『未知生，焉知死？

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'If one does not yet know life, how can one know death?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'If you do not yet understand life, how can you understand death?

sentences.zh: 』安有棄堂堂之政而從鬼教乎！

translations.literal: ' How can there be abandoning the august governance of the living realm to follow the ghost teaching!
translations.idiomatic: How can anyone abandon the bright governance of the living world to follow the doctrine of ghosts!

sentences.zh: 又，今南服未靜，眾役仍煩，百生之情，實多避役，若復聽之，恐捐棄孝慈，比屋皆為沙門矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the south is not yet settled, public corvée remains heavy, and among the hundred classes of the people the feeling is in truth largely one of evading labor; if this is again permitted, I fear filial piety and compassion will be cast aside and every household will become monks.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the south is not yet pacified and corvée remains heavy. Many people seek to evade labor. If this is permitted again, I fear filial piety and compassion will be cast aside and every household will turn monastic.

sentences.zh: 」都統僧暹等忿瑒謂之「鬼教」，以為謗佛，泣訴於太后。

translations.literal: " The chief superintendent monk Seng Xian and others, angered that Yang called it the "ghost teaching," regarded this as slandering the Buddha and wept as they appealed to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Superintendent Monk Seng Xian and others, furious that Yang had called Buddhism the "ghost teaching," accused him of slandering the Buddha and wept before the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后責之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager rebuked Yang.

sentences.zh: 瑒曰：「天曰神，地曰示氏，人曰鬼。

translations.literal: Yang said: "Heaven is called spirit, earth is called the Shi designation, humans are called ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Yang replied, "Heaven is called spirit, earth is called Shi, and humans are called ghosts.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: 'In the bright realm there are rites and music; in the dark realm there are ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, 'In the bright realm are rites and music; in the dark realm are ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 』然則明者為堂堂，幽者為鬼教。

translations.literal: ' Thus what belongs to the bright realm is the august governance, and what belongs to the dark realm is the ghost teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the bright realm is the august world of the living, and the dark realm is the world of ghosts.

sentences.zh: 佛本出於人，名之為鬼，愚謂非謗。

translations.literal: The Buddha originally came forth from humans; to name him a ghost—I humbly believe this is not slander.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha was born a man. To call him a ghost is, I believe, not slander.

sentences.zh: 」太后雖知瑒言為允，難違暹等之意，罰瑒金一兩。

translations.literal: " Though the empress dowager knew Yang's words were reasonable, she found it hard to go against the wishes of Xian and the others, and fined Yang one liang of gold.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager knew Yang was right, but unwilling to defy Seng Xian and the others, she fined him one liang of gold.

sentences.zh: 魏徵南大將軍田益宗求為東豫州刺史，以招二子，太后不許，竟卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: Tian Yizong, Wei Grand General Who Conquers the South, requested appointment as inspector of Eastern Yuzhou in order to summon his two sons; the empress dowager did not grant it, and he ultimately died in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizong, Wei's Grand General Who Conquers the South, asked to be made inspector of Eastern Yuzhou so he could summon his two sons. The empress dowager refused, and he died in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 柔然伏跋可汗，壯健善用兵，是歲，西擊高車，大破之，執其王彌俄突，系其足於駑馬，頓曳殺之，漆其頭為飲器。

translations.literal: Fuba Khan of Rouran, strong and skilled in the use of troops, that year attacked the Gaoche in the west, routed them utterly, seized their king Mie'etuo, tied his feet to a slow horse, dragged him to death, and lacquered his skull to make a drinking vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Fuba Khan of Rouran, vigorous and skilled in war, marched west that year against the Gaoche, crushed them, seized their king Mie'etuo, tied his feet to a draft horse and dragged him to death, then lacquered his skull into a drinking cup.

sentences.zh: 鄰國先羈屬柔然後叛去者，伏跋皆擊滅之，其國復強。

translations.literal: Among neighboring states that had first submitted to Rouran and then rebelled and departed, Fuba struck down and destroyed them all, and his state grew strong again.
translations.idiomatic: Every neighboring state that had once submitted to Rouran and then rebelled, Fuba conquered and destroyed, and his realm grew strong again.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝四天監十六年（

translations.literal: The sixteenth year of Tianjian of Emperor Wu the High Ancestor (
translations.idiomatic: The sixteenth year of Tianjian of Emperor Wu the High Ancestor (

sentences.zh: 丁酉，公元五一七年）

translations.literal: dingyou, 517 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingyou, 517 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinwei, the Emperor performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinwei, the Emperor sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 魏大乘餘賊復相聚，突入瀛州，刺史宇文福之子員外散騎侍郎延帥奴客拒之。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits of the Great Vehicle sect in Wei gathered again, burst into Yingzhou, and Yan, son of Inspector Yuwen Fu and an external attendant gentleman of the Fast Cavalry, led household retainers to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Surviving Great Vehicle rebels in Wei gathered again and broke into Yingzhou. Yan, son of Inspector Yuwen Fu and an external attendant gentleman of the Fast Cavalry, led household retainers to meet them.

sentences.zh: 賊燒齋閣，延突火抱福出外，肌發皆焦，勒眾苦戰，賊遂散走，追討，平之。

translations.literal: The bandits set fire to the fasting hall; Yan burst through the flames, carried Fu out in his arms, flesh and hair all scorched, rallied the men to fight bitterly, and the bandits then scattered and fled; they were pursued and the disturbance was put down.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels set the fasting hall ablaze. Yan charged through the fire, carried his father out in his arms with flesh and hair scorched black, rallied the men to fight on, and drove the rebels off. Pursuit followed and the rebellion was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏初，民間皆不用錢，高祖太和十九年，始鑄太和五銖錢，遣錢工在所鼓鑄。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Wei, the people did not use money at all; in the nineteenth year of Taihe of Emperor Gaozu, the Taihe five-zhu coins were first cast, and coin workers were sent to each place to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wei the people did not use coin at all. In the nineteenth year of Taihe, Emperor Gaozu first cast the Taihe five-zhu coins and sent mint workers to strike them locally.

sentences.zh: 民有欲鑄錢者，聽就官爐，銅必精練，無得淆雜，世宗永平三年，又鑄五銖錢，禁天下用錢不依準式者。

translations.literal: If the people wished to cast coin, they were permitted to go to the official furnaces; the copper had to be finely refined and might not be adulterated. In the third year of Yongping of Emperor Shizong, five-zhu coins were cast again, and the realm was forbidden to use coin that did not conform to the standard regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wished to cast coin were allowed to use the official furnaces, provided the copper was refined and unadulterated. In the third year of Yongping, Emperor Shizong cast five-zhu coins again and forbade the use of coin that did not meet the standard.

sentences.zh: 既而洛陽及諸州鎮所用錢各不同，商貨不通。

translations.literal: Before long the coin used in Luoyang and the various prefectures and garrisons differed from one another, and trade in goods did not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the coin in use at Luoyang and in the various prefectures and garrisons differed, and commerce stalled.

sentences.zh: 尚書令任城王澄上言以為：「不行之錢，律有明式，指謂雞眼、鐶鑿，更無餘禁。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng, director of the Secretariat, submitted a memorial, saying: "As for coin that may not circulate, the law has a clear standard, meaning chicken-eye and ring-chisel coins, and there is no further prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng, director of the Secretariat, argued: "The law clearly defines forbidden coin as chicken-eye and ring-chisel pieces, and forbids nothing else.

sentences.zh: 計河西諸州今所行者悉非制限，昔來繩禁，愚竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Considering that the coin now circulating in the Hexi prefectures is entirely outside the prescribed limits, the long-standing strict prohibition—I humbly find this perplexing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the coin now circulating in the Hexi prefectures falls entirely outside those limits. I am puzzled by this long-standing strict ban.

sentences.zh: 又河北既無新錢，復禁舊者，專以單絲之縑、疏縷之布，狹幅促度，不中常式，裂匹為尺，以濟有無，徒成杼軸之勞，不免饑寒之苦，殆非所以救恤凍餒，子育黎元之意也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Hebei there is no new coin, yet old coin is again forbidden, so that people rely solely on single-thread silk and loosely woven cloth, narrow in width and short in measure, not meeting the usual standard, tearing bolts into feet to meet one another's needs—this only creates the toil of loom and spindle without escaping the suffering of hunger and cold; it is hardly the intent of relieving the frozen and starving and nurturing the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei there is no new coin, yet old coin is forbidden. People must trade in narrow, substandard silk and coarse cloth, tearing bolts into feet to get by. This adds loom-work without easing hunger and cold. It is hardly the way to succor the destitute and nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 錢之為用，貫繈相屬，不假度量，平均簡易，濟世之宜，謂為深允。

translations.literal: Coin as a medium links string to string without need of measuring; it is even, simple, and suited to aiding the age—I deem this deeply fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Coin links value string to string without need of measure. It is even, simple, and well suited to the needs of the age.

sentences.zh: 乞並下諸方州鎮，其太和與新鑄五銖及古諸錢方俗所便用者，但內外全好，雖有大小之異，並得通行，貴賤之差，自依鄉價。

translations.literal: I beg that this be sent down to all prefectures and garrisons: Taihe and newly cast five-zhu coins and all ancient coins that local custom finds convenient to use—provided they are whole and sound inside and out—though they differ in size, may all circulate, with differences in value determined by local price.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this be sent to every prefecture and garrison: Taihe and newly cast five-zhu coins, and any ancient coin local custom favors, provided they are whole and sound, may all circulate regardless of size, with value set by local price.

sentences.zh: 庶貨環海內，公私無壅。

translations.literal: Thus goods may circulate throughout the realm, and public and private interests will not be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Then goods may circulate throughout the realm and neither public nor private trade will be obstructed.

sentences.zh: 其雞眼、鐶鑿及盜鑄、毀大為小、生新巧偽不如法者，據律罪之。

translations.literal: As for chicken-eye and ring-chisel coins, illicit casting, making large coins into small ones, and newly made clever counterfeits not conforming to law—these should be punished according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Chicken-eye and ring-chisel coins, illicit casting, clipping large coins into small ones, and newly made counterfeits should be punished by law.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 然河北少錢，民猶用物交易，錢不入市。

translations.literal: Yet in Hebei there was little coin; the people still traded in goods, and money did not enter the markets.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Hebei coin was scarce; the people still bartered in kind, and cash scarcely circulated in the markets.

sentences.zh: 魏人多竊冒軍功，尚書左丞盧同閱吏部勳書，因加檢核，得竊階者三百餘人，乃奏：「乞總集吏部、中兵二局勳簿，對句奏案，更造兩通，一關吏部，一留兵局。

translations.literal: Many in Wei fraudulently claimed military merit. Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Lu Tong reviewed the Ministry of Personnel's merit records and added scrutiny, finding more than three hundred who had stolen rank. He memorialized: "I request that the merit registers of the Ministry of Personnel and the Central Army Bureau be gathered together, checked against submitted memorial records, and two new copies made—one sent to the Ministry of Personnel, one kept at the Army Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Many in Wei had fraudulently claimed military honors. Lu Tong, Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, reviewed the Ministry of Personnel's merit rolls and tightened scrutiny, uncovering more than three hundred who had stolen rank. He memorialized: "I ask that the merit registers of the Ministry of Personnel and the Central Army Bureau be assembled, checked against submitted memorials, and two new copies made—one for the Ministry of Personnel, one retained at the Army Bureau.

sentences.zh: 又，在軍斬首成一階以上者，即令行台軍司給券，當中豎裂，一支付勳人，一支送門下，以防偽巧。

translations.literal: Moreover, for those who in the army achieved one rank grade or more through decapitation, the field headquarters army office should be ordered to issue certificates, split vertically down the middle—one part given to the merit holder, one part sent to the Gate Department, to guard against fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for anyone in the field who earned one full rank grade or more through decapitations, the field army office should issue certificates, split vertically down the middle—one half to the merit holder, one half to the Gate Department—to prevent forgery.

sentences.zh: 」太后從之。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager assented.

sentences.zh: 同，玄之族孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Tong was a descendant of Lu Xuanzhi's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong was a descendant of Lu Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 中尉無匡奏請取景明元年已來，內外考簿、吏部除書、中兵勳案、並諸殿最，欲以案校竊階盜官之人，太后許之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Wu Kuang memorialized requesting records from Jingming era year 1 onward—the internal and external examination registers, Ministry of Personnel appointment documents, Central Army merit files, and all evaluations—to verify those who fraudulently claimed rank and stole office. The empress dowager granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wu Kuang memorialized asking that from the first year of the Jingming era onward all internal and external examination registers, Ministry of Personnel appointment documents, Central Army merit files, and performance evaluations be gathered to verify those who had stolen rank and office. The empress dowager approved.

sentences.zh: 尚書令任城王澄表以為：「法忌煩苛，治貴清約。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Prince Cheng of Ren Cheng submitted a memorial stating: "Law shuns cumbersomeness and severity; governance values clarity and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Prince Cheng of Ren Cheng submitted a memorial arguing: "Law abhors fussiness and severity; good governance prizes clarity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 御史之體，風聞是司，若聞有冒勳妄階，止應攝其一簿，研檢虛實，繩以典刑。

translations.literal: The proper role of censors is to hear reports on the wind; if there is word of false merit and reckless rank-seeking, they should take only one register, investigate truth and falsity, and punish according to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Censors exist to hear what the wind carries; if word comes of false merit and reckless rank-seeking, they should seize only one register, sift truth from falsehood, and punish according to statute.

sentences.zh: 豈有移一省之案，尋兩紀之事，如此求過，誰諶其罪！

translations.literal: How can one transfer a whole province's files to hunt for matters spanning two reign-periods? Such fault-seeking—who could bear the guilt!
translations.idiomatic: How can one move an entire province's archives to hunt for matters spanning two reign-periods? Fault-seeking on such a scale—who could bear the guilt!

sentences.zh: 斯實聖朝所宜重慎也。

translations.literal: This is indeed something our sage dynasty ought to weigh with utmost caution.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely what our sage dynasty ought to treat with the greatest caution.

sentences.zh: 」太后乃止。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager then stopped [the inquiry].
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager then halted the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 又以匡所言數不從，慮其辭解，欲獎安之，乃加鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Also, because Wu Kuang's advice had often been rejected, fearing he might resign, wishing to reward and reassure him, [she] promoted him to General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wu Kuang's counsel had repeatedly been rejected, the empress dowager feared he might resign and wished to reward and reassure him; she therefore promoted him to General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁未，立匡為東平王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingwei, Wu Kuang was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingwei, Wu Kuang was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙子，敕織官，文錦不得為仙人鳥善之形，為其裁剪，有乖仁恕。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingzi, [an edict] ordered weavers that patterned brocade must not take the forms of immortals, birds, or beasts, for cutting cloth thus departed from benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingzi, an edict ordered the weaving offices that figured brocade must not depict immortals, birds, or beasts, for such cutting of cloth violated benevolence and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏廣平文穆王懷卒。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Huai, Prince Wenmu of Guangping of Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Huai, Prince Wenmu of Guangping of Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊申，魏以中書監胡國珍為司徒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wushen, Wei made Hu Guozhen, supervisor of the Secretariat, Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wushen, Wei appointed Hu Guozhen, supervisor of the Secretariat, Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 詔以宗廟用牲，有累冥道，宜皆以面為之。

translations.literal: An edict held that using sacrificial animals in the ancestral temple burdened the dark path; all [offerings] should be made of flour instead.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that using sacrificial animals in the ancestral temple burdened the realm of the dead; all offerings should instead be made of dough.

sentences.zh: 於是朝野喧嘩，以為宗廟去牲，乃是不復血食，帝竟不從。

translations.literal: At this the court and commoners alike raised a clamor, deeming that removing animals from the ancestral temple meant no longer offering blood sacrifice; the emperor in the end did not follow [this view].
translations.idiomatic: At this the court and countryside erupted in uproar, taking the removal of sacrificial animals from the ancestral temple to mean an end to blood offerings; the emperor in the end did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 八坐乃議以大脯代一元大武。

translations.literal: The Eight Ministers then deliberated using large dried meat in place of the primary sacrificial ox.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Ministers then debated substituting large dried meat for the primary sacrificial ox.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丁未，詔魏太師高陽王雍入居門下，參決尚書奏事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on dingwei, an edict ordered Grand Preceptor Prince Yong of Gaoyang of Wei to enter and reside at the Gate Department to participate in deciding Secretariat memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on dingwei, an edict ordered Grand Preceptor Prince Yong of Gaoyang of Wei to take up residence at the Gate Department and join in deciding Secretariat memorials.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，詔以宗廟猶用脯脩，更議代之，於是以大餅代大脯，其餘盡用蔬果。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, an edict [noted that] the ancestral temple still used dried and salted meat; after further deliberation on substitutes, large cakes replaced large dried meat, and the rest were entirely fruits and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, an edict noted that the ancestral temple still used dried and salted meats; after further debate on substitutes, large cakes replaced the large dried meat, and everything else was fruits and vegetables.

sentences.zh: 又起至敬殿、景陽台，置七廟座，每月中再設淨饌。

translations.literal: Also [they] raised the Hall of Utmost Reverence and the Jingyang Terrace, set up seven temple seats, and twice each month at mid-month offered pure vegetarian fare.
translations.idiomatic: They also built the Hall of Utmost Reverence and the Jingyang Terrace, established seven temple seats, and twice each month at mid-month set out pure vegetarian offerings.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏詔：北京士民未遷者，悉聽留居為永業。

translations.literal: On yimao, Wei issued an edict: those northerners at Beijing who had not yet relocated were all permitted to remain and settle as permanent holdings.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Wei issued an edict: northerners at Beijing who had not yet moved were all permitted to remain and hold their lands in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲子，巴州刺史牟漢寵叛，降魏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, Mou Hanchong, inspector of Bazhou, rebelled and surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, Mou Hanchong, inspector of Bazhou, rebelled and surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，柔然伏跋可汗遣俟近尉比建等請和於魏，用敵國之禮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Fuba Khan of Rouran sent Akin Yubi Jian and others to seek peace with Wei, using the etiquette due between equal states.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Fuba Khan of Rouran sent Akin Yubi Jian and others to sue for peace with Wei, using the etiquette owed between equal states.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以右衛將軍馮道根為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: That year, Right Guard General Feng Daogen was made inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Right Guard General Feng Daogen was appointed inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 道根謹厚木訥，行軍能檢敕士卒；

translations.literal: Daogen was careful, honest, and taciturn, and on campaign could restrain and command his soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Daogen was careful, honest, and sparing of speech, and on campaign could discipline his soldiers;

sentences.zh: 諸將爭功，道根獨默然。

translations.literal: when the generals vied for credit, Daogen alone remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: when the other generals vied for credit, Daogen alone kept silent.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，吏民懷之。

translations.literal: In governance he was clear and sparing, and officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was plain and restrained, and officials and commoners alike cherished him.

sentences.zh: 上嘗歎曰：「道根所在，令朝廷不復憶有一州。

translations.literal: The emperor once sighed and said: "Wherever Daogen is stationed, he makes the court forget it even has a province there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sighed and said, "Wherever Daogen serves, he makes the court forget it even has a province there.

sentences.zh: 」魏尚書崔亮奏請於王屋等山採銅鑄錢，從之。

translations.literal: " Secretary Cui Liang of Wei memorialized requesting copper be mined on Mount Wangwu and elsewhere to cast coin; [the court] approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Secretary Cui Liang of Wei memorialized asking that copper be mined on Mount Wangwu and elsewhere to cast coin; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 是後民多私鑄，錢稍薄小，用之益輕。

translations.literal: After this the people largely cast coin privately; money grew somewhat thinner and smaller, and in use it weighed even less.
translations.idiomatic: After this the people widely cast coin in secret; the currency grew thinner and smaller, and in circulation weighed even less.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝四天監十七年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Great Ancestor, seventeenth year of Tianjian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu the Great Ancestor, seventeenth year of Tianjian (
