translations.literal: wuxu, AD 518)
translations.idiomatic: wuxu, AD 518)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲子，魏以氐酋楊定為陰平王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiazi, Wei made the Di chieftain Yang Ding Prince of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiazi, Wei enfeoffed the Di chieftain Yang Ding as Prince of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 魏秦州羌反。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Qinzhou in Wei rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang of Qinzhou in Wei rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸巳，安成康王秀卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gisi, Xiu, Prince Kang of Ancheng, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gisi, Xiu, Prince Kang of Ancheng, died.

sentences.zh: 秀雖與上布衣昆弟，及為君臣，小心畏敬過於疏賤，上益以此賢之。

translations.literal: Though Xiu had been the emperor's brother in common cloth, once they became sovereign and subject his cautious reverence exceeded that of distant inferiors, and the emperor all the more esteemed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiu had been the emperor's brother in plain cloth, once they became sovereign and subject his cautious reverence exceeded that shown by distant inferiors, and the emperor all the more admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 秀與弟始興王憺尤相友愛，憺久為荊州刺史，常中分其祿以給秀，秀稱心受之，亦不辭多也。

translations.literal: Xiu and his younger brother Prince Shi of Shixing were especially close; Shi long served as inspector of Jingzhou and habitually divided his salary in half to give Xiu; Xiu accepted with satisfaction and did not refuse even when the share was large.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and his younger brother Prince Shi of Shixing were especially devoted to each other. Shi long served as inspector of Jingzhou and habitually divided his salary in half for Xiu; Xiu accepted gladly and never refused even when the share was large.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiachen, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏大赦，改元神龜。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Wei granted a general amnesty and changed the era name to Shengui.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Wei granted a general amnesty and changed the era name to Shengui.

sentences.zh: 魏東益州氐反。

translations.literal: The Di of Eastern Yizhou in Wei rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Di of Eastern Yizhou in Wei rebelled.

sentences.zh: 魏主引見柔然使者，讓之以籓禮不備，議依漢待匈奴故事，遣使報之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler summoned and received the Rouran envoys, reproached them for incomplete vassal etiquette, and debated following the Han precedent for treating the Xiongnu, dispatching envoys in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler received the Rouran envoys in audience, reproached them for incomplete vassal etiquette, and debated following the Han precedent for treating the Xiongnu, dispatching envoys in reply.

sentences.zh: 司農少卿張倫上表，以為：「太祖經啟帝圖，日有不暇，遂令豎子遊魂一方。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chamber of Agriculture Zhang Lun submitted a memorial stating: "The Founding Emperor was opening the imperial design and had not a day to spare, so a mere upstart was left to wander one region like a stray soul.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Chamber of Agriculture Zhang Lun submitted a memorial arguing: "The Founding Emperor was opening the imperial design and had not a day to spare, so a mere upstart was left to wander one corner of the realm like a stray soul.

sentences.zh: 亦由中國多虞，急諸華而緩夷狄也。

translations.literal: This also arose because China faced many alarms—we pressed the Huaxia peoples and relaxed toward the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: This also came of China's many alarms—we pressed the Huaxia peoples and relaxed toward the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 高祖方事南轅，未遑北伐。

translations.literal: The Great Ancestor was then engaged on the southern frontier and had no leisure for northern campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Ancestor was then engaged on the southern frontier and had no leisure for northern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 世宗述遵遺志，虜使之來，受而弗答。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong followed and carried out his legacy; when barbarian envoys came, [he] received them yet made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong followed and carried out his legacy; when barbarian envoys came, he received them yet made no reply.

sentences.zh: 以為大明臨御，國富兵強，抗敵之禮，何憚而為之，何求而行之！

translations.literal: [He] held that with brilliant majesty presiding, the state rich and armies strong, the etiquette owed between equal rivals—why fear to use it, why scheme to employ it!
translations.idiomatic: He held that with brilliant majesty presiding, the state rich and armies strong, the etiquette owed between equal rivals—why shrink from it, why scheme to use it!

sentences.zh: 今虜雖慕德而來，亦欲觀我強弱；

translations.literal: Now though the barbarians come admiring our virtue, they also wish to observe our strength and weakness;
translations.idiomatic: Now though the barbarians come admiring our virtue, they also wish to gauge our strength and weakness;

sentences.zh: 若使王人銜命虜庭，與為昆弟，恐非祖宗之意也。

translations.literal: if we sent royal envoys bearing credentials to the barbarian court and treated them as brothers, that would likely not accord with the intent of our ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: if we sent royal envoys bearing credentials to the barbarian court and treated them as brothers, that would likely not accord with the intent of our ancestors.

sentences.zh: 苟事不獲已，應為制詔，示以上下之儀，命宰臣致書，諭以歸順之道，觀其從違，徐以恩威進退之，則王者之體正矣。

translations.literal: If the matter cannot be avoided, an imperial edict should be issued showing the etiquette between superior and inferior; leading ministers should be ordered to send letters expounding the way of submission; their compliance or defiance should be watched, and slowly reward and punishment applied to advance or retreat—then the proper bearing of a king would be correct.
translations.idiomatic: If the matter cannot be avoided, an imperial edict should show the etiquette between superior and inferior; leading ministers should be ordered to send letters expounding the way of submission; their compliance or defiance should be watched, and slowly reward and punishment applied to advance or retreat—then the proper bearing of a king would be restored.

sentences.zh: 豈可以戎狄兼併，而遽虧典禮乎！

translations.literal: How can one, because barbarians happen to gather and submit, abruptly damage canonical ritual!
translations.idiomatic: How can one, because barbarians happen to gather and submit, abruptly damage canonical ritual!

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " [The emperor] did not follow [this advice].
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 倫，白澤之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Lun was the son of Bai Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun was the son of Bai Ze.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛未，魏靈壽武敬公於忠卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinwei, Yu Zhong, Duke Wu-Jing of Lingshou of Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinwei, Yu Zhong, Duke Wu-Jing of Lingshou of Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 魏南秦州氐反。

translations.literal: The Di of Southern Qinzhou in Wei rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Di of Southern Qinzhou in Wei rebelled.

sentences.zh: 遣龍驤將軍崔襲持節諭之。

translations.literal: [The court] sent Dragon Prancing General Cui Xi with staff of authority to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Dragon Prancing General Cui Xi with staff of authority to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁酉，魏秦文宣公胡國珍卒，贈假黃鉞、相國、都督中外諸軍事、太師，號曰太上秦公，加九錫，葬以殊禮，贈襚儀衛，事極優厚。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingyou, Hu Guozhen, Duke Wen-Xuan of Qin of Wei, died; he was posthumously granted the ceremonial axe, the title of chief minister, command over all armies internal and external, and Grand Preceptor; he was styled Grand Preceptor Duke of Qin, given the Nine Bestowments, buried with extraordinary rites, and granted funeral robes, honors, and guard—every detail was utmost in favor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingyou, Hu Guozhen, Duke Wen-Xuan of Qin of Wei, died. He was posthumously granted the ceremonial axe, the title of chief minister, command over all armies internal and external, and Grand Preceptor; styled Grand Preceptor Duke of Qin; given the Nine Bestowments; buried with extraordinary rites; and granted funeral robes, honors, and guard—every favor was pushed to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 又迎太后母皇甫氏之柩與國珍合葬，謂之太上秦孝穆君。

translations.literal: Also [they] brought the coffin of the empress dowager's mother, Lady Huangfu, to be buried jointly with Guozhen, calling them the Grand Preceptor Duke and Duchess of Qin, Xiao-Mu.
translations.idiomatic: They also brought the coffin of the empress dowager's mother, Lady Huangfu, to be buried with Guozhen, styling the pair the Grand Preceptor Duke and Duchess of Qin, Xiao-Mu.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫常山張普惠以為前世後父無稱「太上」者，「太上」之名不可施於人臣，詣闕上疏陳之，左右莫敢為通。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Advisor Zhang Puhui of Changshan held that in former ages stepfathers of emperors were never styled "Grand Preceptor"; the title "Grand Preceptor" must not be applied to a subject; he went to the palace and submitted a memorial stating this, but those around him dared not pass it through.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Advisor Zhang Puhui of Changshan held that in former ages stepfathers of emperors were never styled "Grand Preceptor"; that title must not be applied to a subject. He went to the palace and submitted a memorial stating this, but those around him dared not pass it through.

sentences.zh: 會胡氏穿壙，下有磐石，乃密表，以為：「天無二日，土無二王，『太上』者因『上』而生名也，皇太后稱『令』以系『敕』下，蓋取三從之道，遠同文母列於十亂，今司徒為『太上』，恐乖系敕之意。

translations.literal: When the Hu clan was digging the tomb chamber and encountered bedrock below, he submitted a secret memorial stating: "Heaven has not two suns; earth has not two kings. 'Grand Preceptor' is a title derived from 'superior'; the empress dowager uses 'Order' linked to 'Edict' in issuance—roughly the way of threefold submission, remotely akin to King Wen's mother among the Ten Disorders. Now the Minister of Education is styled 'Grand Preceptor'—I fear this conflicts with the intent of binding orders to edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu clan was digging the tomb chamber and struck bedrock below, he submitted a secret memorial stating: "Heaven has not two suns; earth has not two kings. 'Grand Preceptor' is a title derived from 'superior'; the empress dowager uses 'Order' linked to 'Edict' in issuance—roughly the way of threefold submission, remotely akin to King Wen's mother among the Ten Disorders. Now the Minister of Education is styled 'Grand Preceptor'—I fear this conflicts with the intent of binding orders to edicts.

sentences.zh: 孔子稱：『必也正名乎！

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'One must rectify names!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: 'One must rectify names!

sentences.zh: 』比克吉定兆，而以淺改卜，亦或天地神靈所以垂至戒、啟聖情也。

translations.literal: ' Now that an auspicious date and site have been fixed, yet the divination is changed for a shallow reason—perhaps this is heaven, earth, and the spirits delivering a supreme warning and opening the sage heart.
translations.idiomatic: ' Now that an auspicious date and site have been fixed, yet the divination is changed for a shallow reason—perhaps this is heaven, earth, and the spirits delivering a supreme warning and opening the sage heart.

sentences.zh: 伏願停逼上之號，以邀廉光之福。

translations.literal: I humbly wish to stop the forced use of the 'superior' title, to seek the blessing of modest integrity.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish to stop the forced use of the 'superior' title, to seek the blessing of modest integrity.

sentences.zh: 」太后乃親至國珍宅，召集五品以上博議。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager then personally came to Guozhen's residence and summoned officials of fifth rank and above for broad deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager then personally came to Guozhen's residence and summoned officials of fifth rank and above for broad deliberation.

sentences.zh: 王公皆希太后意，爭詰難普惠；

translations.literal: Princes and ministers all courted the empress dowager's intent and vied to cross-examine Puhui;
translations.idiomatic: Princes and ministers all courted the empress dowager's intent and vied to cross-examine Puhui;

sentences.zh: 普惠應機辨析，無能屈者。

translations.literal: Puhui answered according to each challenge, and none could refute him.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui answered each challenge as it came, and none could refute him.

sentences.zh: 太后使元叉宣令於普惠曰：「朕之所行，孝子之志。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had Yuan Cha proclaim to Puhui: "What I do is the mind of a filial child.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had Yuan Cha proclaim to Puhui: "What I do is the mind of a filial child.

sentences.zh: 卿之所陳，忠臣之道。

translations.literal: What you state is the way of a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: What you state is the way of a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 群公已有成議，卿不得苦奪朕懷。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers already have a settled decision; you must not bitterly wrest my mind.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers already have a settled decision; you must not bitterly wrest my mind.

sentences.zh: 後有所見，勿難言也。

translations.literal: If hereafter you have views, do not hesitate to speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: If hereafter you have views, do not hesitate to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 太后為太上君造寺，壯麗埒於永寧。

translations.literal: The empress dowager built a temple for the Grand Preceptor Duke and Duchess; its grandeur rivaled Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager built a temple for the Grand Preceptor Duke and Duchess; its grandeur rivaled Yongning.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏復征民綿麻之稅，張普惠上疏，以為：「高祖廢大鬥，去長尺，改重稱，以愛民薄賦。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized to renew the tax on hemp and silk from the people; Zhang Puhui submitted a memorial stating: "The Great Ancestor abolished the large peck-measure, removed the extended foot-rule, and changed the heavy weight-standard, to love the people and lighten taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat memorialized to renew the tax on hemp and silk from the people. Zhang Puhui submitted a memorial arguing: "The Great Ancestor abolished the large peck-measure, removed the extended foot-rule, and changed the heavy weight-standard, to love the people and lighten taxes.

sentences.zh: 知軍國須綿麻之用，故於絹增稅綿八兩，於布增稅麻十五斤，民以稱尺所減，不啻綿麻，故鼓舞供調。

translations.literal: Knowing that army and state required hemp and silk, he therefore added to silk cloth a tax of eight ounces of silk, and to hemp cloth a tax of fifteen pounds of hemp; the people found what the scales and measures had cut more than matched the hemp and silk levy, so they went gladly to supply tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that army and state required hemp and silk, he therefore added to silk cloth a tax of eight ounces of silk, and to hemp cloth a tax of fifteen pounds of hemp; the people found what the scales and measures had cut more than matched the hemp and silk levy, so they went gladly to supply tribute.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，所稅絹布，浸復長闊，百姓嗟怨，聞於朝野。

translations.literal: From then until now, the silk and cloth taxed have gradually grown longer and wider again; the people sigh in resentment, and it is heard throughout court and country.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now, the silk and cloth taxed have gradually grown longer and wider again; the people sigh in resentment, and word of it fills court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 宰輔不尋其本在於幅廣度長，遽罷綿麻。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, not tracing the root cause to excessive width and length, abruptly abolished the hemp and silk tax.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, not tracing the root cause to excessive width and length, abruptly abolished the hemp and silk tax.

sentences.zh: 既而尚書以國用不足，復欲征斂。

translations.literal: Before long the Secretariat, citing insufficient state revenue, again wished to levy collections.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Secretariat, citing insufficient state revenue, again wished to levy collections.

sentences.zh: 去天下之大信，棄己行之成詔，追前之非，遂後三史。

translations.literal: To cast off the great faith of the realm, abandon an edict already in force, pursue past errors, and then fall behind the Three Histories—
translations.idiomatic: To cast off the great faith of the realm, abandon an edict already in force, pursue past errors, and then fall behind the Three Histories—

sentences.zh: 不思庫中有大麻，而群臣共竊之也，何則所輸之物，或斤羨百銖，未聞有司依律以罪州郡；

translations.literal: not to reflect that though the storehouses held ample hemp, ministers together skimmed it—how so? Goods submitted were sometimes a hundred zhu overweight per jin, yet never did officials hear of punishing prefectures and commanderies according to law;
translations.idiomatic: and not to reflect that though the storehouses held ample hemp, ministers together skimmed it—how so? Goods submitted were sometimes a hundred zhu overweight per jin, yet never did officials hear of punishing prefectures and commanderies according to law;

sentences.zh: 或小有濫惡，則坐戶主，連及三長。

translations.literal: yet if there was even slight inferior quality, the household head was held liable, and the three heads [of the mutual-responsibility system] were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: yet if there was even slight inferior quality, the household head was held liable, and the three heads of the mutual-responsibility system were implicated.

sentences.zh: 是以在庫絹布，逾制者多，郡臣受俸，人求長闊厚重，無復準極，未聞以端幅有餘還求輸官者也。

translations.literal: Thus stored silk and cloth exceeding standards grew numerous; commandery officials receiving salary, people sought length, width, and weight without standard or limit—never was it heard that surplus from proper bolt-width was returned and demanded back for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thus stored silk and cloth exceeding standards grew numerous; commandery officials on salary, people sought length, width, and weight without standard or limit—never was it heard that surplus from proper bolt-width was returned and demanded back for the state.

sentences.zh: 今欲復調綿麻，當先正稱、尺，明立嚴禁，無得放溢，使天下知二聖之心愛民惜法如此，則太和之政復見於神龜矣。

translations.literal: Now if you wish again to levy hemp and silk, you should first rectify weights and measures, clearly establish strict prohibitions, and allow no excess—so all under heaven will know both sage rulers' hearts love the people and prize law thus; then the governance of Tahe would reappear in Shengui.
translations.idiomatic: Now if you wish again to levy hemp and silk, you should first rectify weights and measures, clearly establish strict prohibitions, and allow no excess—so all under heaven will know both sage rulers' hearts love the people and prize law thus; then the governance of Tahe would reappear in Shengui.

sentences.zh: 普惠又以魏主好游騁苑囿，不親視朝，過崇佛法，郊廟之事多委有司，上疏切諫，以為：「殖不思之冥業，損巨費於生民，減祿削力，近供無事之僧，崇飾雲殿，遠邀未然之報，昧爽之臣稽首於外，玄寂之眾遨遊於內，衍禮忤時，人靈未穆。

translations.literal: Puhui also, because the Wei ruler loved roaming parks and preserves, did not personally attend court, excessively honored Buddhism, and largely delegated suburban and temple affairs to subordinate officials, submitted a sharp memorial remonstrating: "You cultivate heedless dark karma, drain vast expense from the living people, cut salaries and labor, supply idle monks nearby, build and adorn cloud-halls afar to invite unearned reward; at dawn ministers kowtow outside while the silent multitude roams within; ritual spreads against the season—humans and spirits are not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui also, because the Wei ruler loved roaming parks and preserves, did not personally attend court, excessively honored Buddhism, and largely delegated suburban and temple affairs to subordinate officials, submitted a sharp memorial remonstrating: "You cultivate heedless dark karma, drain vast expense from the living people, cut salaries and labor, supply idle monks nearby, build and adorn cloud-halls afar to invite unearned reward; at dawn ministers kowtow outside while the silent multitude roams within; ritual spreads against the season—humans and spirits are not at peace.

sentences.zh: 愚謂修朝夕之因，求示氏劫之果，未若收萬國之歡心以事其親，使天下和平，災害不生也。

translations.literal: This fool holds that tending morning-and-evening merit to seek fruits shown across kalpas is not equal to gathering the hearts of all lands to serve one's parents, so that all under heaven is at peace and calamities do not arise.
translations.idiomatic: This fool holds that tending morning-and-evening merit to seek fruits shown across kalpas is not equal to gathering the hearts of all lands to serve one's parents, so that all under heaven is at peace and calamities do not arise.

sentences.zh: 伏願淑慎威儀，為萬邦作式，躬致郊廟之虔，親紆朔望之禮，釋奠成均，竭心千畝。

translations.literal: I humbly wish [Your Majesty] would cultivate dignified, cautious bearing as model for myriad states, personally perform suburban and temple devotions, personally observe new- and full-moon rites, offer sacrifices at the imperial academy, and pour heart into the thousand-acre field.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish Your Majesty would cultivate dignified, cautious bearing as model for myriad states, personally perform suburban and temple devotions, personally observe new- and full-moon rites, offer sacrifices at the imperial academy, and pour heart into the thousand-acre field.

sentences.zh: 量撤僧寺不急之華，還復百官久折之秩。

translations.literal: Measure out and cut the needless splendor of monasteries, and restore the long-reduced ranks of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Measure out and cut the needless splendor of monasteries, and restore the long-reduced ranks of the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 已造者務令簡約速成，未造者一切不復更為。

translations.literal: What is already built should be made plain and finished quickly; what is not yet built should not be undertaken anew at all.
translations.idiomatic: What is already built should be made plain and finished quickly; what is not yet built should not be undertaken anew at all.

sentences.zh: 則孝弟可以通神明，德教可以光四海，節用愛人，法俗俱賴矣。

translations.literal: Then filial piety and brotherliness may reach gods and spirits, virtue and teaching may shine over the four seas, thrift and love of people would be relied on by law and custom alike.
translations.idiomatic: Then filial piety and brotherliness may reach gods and spirits, virtue and teaching may shine over the four seas, and thrift and love of people would be relied on by law and custom alike.

sentences.zh: 」尋敕外議釋奠之禮，又自是每月一陛見群臣，皆用普惠之言也。

translations.literal: " Soon an edict ordered discussion outside the court of the academy sacrifice rite; from then on too he once each month received ministers in audience—all following Puhui's words.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon an edict ordered discussion outside the court of the academy sacrifice rite; from then on he also once each month received ministers in audience—all following Puhui's words.

sentences.zh: 普惠復表論時政得失，太后與帝引普惠於宣光殿，隨事詰難。

translations.literal: Puhui again submitted a memorial discussing gains and losses of current policy; the empress dowager and emperor summoned Puhui to the Xuanguang Hall and questioned and challenged him on each point.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui again submitted a memorial discussing gains and losses of current policy; the empress dowager and emperor summoned Puhui to the Xuanguang Hall and questioned and challenged him on each point.

sentences.zh: 臨川王宏妾弟吳法壽殺人而匿於宏府中，上敕宏出之，即日伏辜。

translations.literal: Prince Hong of Linchuan's younger brother by a concubine, Wu Fashou, killed a man and hid in Hong's residence; the emperor ordered Hong to surrender him, and the same day he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hong of Linchuan's younger brother by a concubine, Wu Fashou, killed a man and hid in Hong's residence; the emperor ordered Hong to surrender him, and the same day he was executed.

sentences.zh: 南司奏免宏官，上注曰：「愛宏者兄弟私親，免宏者王者正法。

translations.literal: The southern bureau memorialized to dismiss Hong from office; the emperor annotated: "To love Hong is the private kinship of brothers; to dismiss Hong is the king's proper law.
translations.idiomatic: The southern bureau memorialized to dismiss Hong from office; the emperor annotated: "To love Hong is the private kinship of brothers; to dismiss Hong is the king's proper law.

sentences.zh: 所奏可。

translations.literal: Your memorial is approved.
translations.idiomatic: Your memorial is approved.

sentences.zh: 」五月，戊寅，司徒、驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史臨川王宏免。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month, on wuyin, Hong, Prince of Linchuan—Minister of Education, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and inspector of Yangzhou—was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month, on wuyin, Hong, Prince of Linchuan—Minister of Education, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and inspector of Yangzhou—was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宏自洛口之敗，常懷愧憤，都下每有竊發，輒以宏為名，屢為有司所奏，上每赦之。

translations.literal: Since his defeat at Luokou, Hong had constantly nursed shame and rage; whenever theft or violence broke out in the capital, the culprits named Hong; he was repeatedly memorialized against by officials, and each time the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Since his defeat at Luokou, Hong had constantly nursed shame and rage; whenever theft or violence broke out in the capital, the culprits named Hong; he was repeatedly memorialized against by officials, and each time the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 上幸光宅寺，有盜伏於驃騎航，待上夜出；

translations.literal: The emperor visited Guangzai Temple; a thief lay in wait at the Piaoqi Bridge, waiting for the emperor to go out at night;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Guangzai Temple; a thief lay in wait at the Piaoqi Bridge, waiting for the emperor to go out at night;

sentences.zh: 上將行，心動，乃於朱雀航過。

translations.literal: as the emperor was about to go, his heart stirred, and he crossed instead by the Zhuque Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: as the emperor was about to go, his heart stirred, and he crossed instead by the Zhuque Bridge.

sentences.zh: 事發，稱為宏所使，上泣謂宏曰：「我人才勝汝百倍，當此猶恐不堪，汝何為者？

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, [the thief] claimed he was sent by Hong; the emperor wept and said to Hong: "My talent surpasses yours a hundredfold, and even I still fear I could not bear this—what are you trying to do?
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, the thief claimed he was sent by Hong; the emperor wept and said to Hong, "My talent surpasses yours a hundredfold, and even I still fear I could not bear this—what are you trying to do?

sentences.zh: 我非不能為漢文帝，念汝愚耳！

translations.literal: It is not that I cannot be like Emperor Wen of Han—I only think you foolish!
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I cannot act like Emperor Wen of Han—I only think you a fool!

sentences.zh: 」宏頓首稱無之；

translations.literal: " Hong kowtowed and said there was nothing to it;
translations.idiomatic: " Hong kowtowed and denied it;

sentences.zh: 故因匿法壽免宏官。

translations.literal: Therefore because he concealed Fashou, Hong was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, because he had concealed Fashou, Hong was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 宏奢僭過度，殖貨無厭。

translations.literal: Hong was extravagant beyond due measure and amassed wealth without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Hong lived in extravagant excess beyond his station and amassed wealth without end.

sentences.zh: 庫屋垂百間，在內堂之後，關籥甚嚴，有疑是鎧仗者，密以聞。

translations.literal: Storehouses numbered nearly a hundred rooms behind the inner hall; the locks were very strict; some suspected they held armor and weapons and secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly a hundred storehouse rooms stood behind the inner hall, locked with the strictest care. Some suspected they held armor and weapons and secretly reported it.

sentences.zh: 上於友愛甚厚，殊不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor's fraternal affection was very deep, yet he was especially displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's brotherly affection ran very deep, yet he was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 佗日，送盛饌與宏愛妾江氏曰：「當來就汝歡宴。

translations.literal: Another day he sent a lavish feast to Hong's beloved concubine, Lady Jiang, saying: "I shall come share your merry banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he sent a lavish feast to Hong's beloved concubine, Lady Jiang, saying, "I shall come and feast with you.

sentences.zh: 」獨攜故人射聲校尉丘佗卿往，與宏及江大飲，半醉後，謂曰：』我今欲履行汝後房。

translations.literal: " Alone he took his old friend Qiu Tuoqing, Commandant of Bowmen Archers, and went; they drank heavily with Hong and Jiang; half drunk, he said: 'Today I wish to walk through your rear chambers.
translations.idiomatic: " He went alone, taking his old friend Qiu Tuoqing, Commandant of Bowmen Archers. He drank heavily with Hong and Jiang, and half drunk said, 'Today I mean to walk through your rear chambers.

sentences.zh: 」即呼輿徑往堂後。

translations.literal: " Immediately he called for a carriage and went straight to the rear of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He at once called for a carriage and went straight to the rear of the hall.

sentences.zh: 宏恐上見其貨賄，顏色怖懼。

translations.literal: Hong feared the emperor would see his hoarded goods; his face showed terror.
translations.idiomatic: Hong feared the emperor would see his hoarded treasure; terror showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 上意益疑之，於是屋屋檢視，每錢百萬為一聚，黃榜標之，千萬為一庫，懸一紫標，如此三十餘間。

translations.literal: The emperor's suspicion deepened; he then inspected room by room—every million coins piled together bore a yellow placard, every ten million filled a storehouse marked with a purple label, thus for more than thirty rooms.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's suspicion only deepened. He inspected room after room: every million coins piled together bore a yellow placard; every ten million filled a storehouse marked with a purple label—more than thirty rooms in all.

sentences.zh: 上與佗卿屈指計，見錢三億餘萬，餘屋貯布絹絲綿漆蜜絲寧蠟等雜貨，但見滿庫，不知多少。

translations.literal: The emperor and Tuoqing counted on their fingers and found more than three hundred million in coin; the remaining rooms stored cloth, silk, floss, lacquer, honey, sericulture wax, and other assorted goods—every storehouse full, the amount unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Tuoqing counted on their fingers and found more than three hundred million in coin. The remaining rooms held cloth, silk, floss, lacquer, honey, wax, and other goods—storehouse after storehouse packed full, with no knowing how much.

sentences.zh: 上始知非仗，大悅，謂曰：「阿六，汝生計大可！

translations.literal: The emperor then knew it was not arms; greatly pleased, he said: "Ah Liu, your livelihood is mighty fine!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then knew it was not arms. Greatly pleased, he said, "Ah Liu, your livelihood is mighty fine!

sentences.zh: 」乃更劇飲至夜，舉燭而還。

translations.literal: " Then they drank even more heavily until night, raised torches, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Then they drank even harder until night, raised torches, and returned.

sentences.zh: 兄弟方更敦睦。

translations.literal: The brothers then became all the more harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers then grew all the closer.

sentences.zh: 宏都下有數十邸，出懸錢立券，每以田宅邸店懸上文契，期訖，便驅券主，奪其宅。

translations.literal: Hong had dozens of lodges in the capital; he issued suspended-money coupons, each time posting house and shop title deeds as collateral on the contract; when the term expired, he drove off the coupon holder and seized the house.
translations.idiomatic: Hong kept dozens of lodges in the capital. He issued suspended-money coupons, posting house and shop title deeds as collateral on each contract; when the term expired, he drove off the holder and seized the property.

sentences.zh: 都下、東土百姓，失業非一。

translations.literal: Common people in the capital and the eastern regions lost livelihoods—not a few.
translations.idiomatic: Common people in the capital and the eastern regions lost their livelihoods—more than a few.

sentences.zh: 上後知之，制懸券不得復驅奪，自此始。

translations.literal: The emperor later learned of it; he decreed suspended coupons might no longer be used to drive out and seize—this began then.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later learned of it, he decreed that suspended coupons could no longer be used to drive people out and seize their property. That prohibition began then.

sentences.zh: 侍中、領軍將軍吳平侯昺，雅有風力，為上所重，軍國大事皆與議決，以為安右將軍，監揚州。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, General Who Leads the Army, Marquis of Wuping Bing—he had natural force of character and was esteemed by the emperor; all great military and state affairs were deliberated and decided with him; he was made General Who Pacifies the Right and overseer of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and General Who Leads the Army, Marquis of Wuping Bing, had natural force of character and was held in high regard by the emperor. All great military and state affairs were deliberated and decided with him. He was made General Who Pacifies the Right and overseer of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 昺自以越親居揚州，涕泣懇讓，上不許。

translations.literal: Bing himself, taking it that as a younger relative he held Yangzhou, wept and earnestly declined; the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Bing himself, feeling it improper that a younger kinsman should hold Yangzhou, wept and earnestly declined; the emperor would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 在州尤稱明斷，符教嚴整。

translations.literal: In the province he was especially noted for clarity in judgment; his dispatch orders were strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he was especially praised for clear judgment; his orders were strict and well kept.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以宏為中軍將軍、中書監，六月，乙酉，又以本號行司徒。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Hong was made General of the Central Army and supervisor of the Secretariat; in the sixth month, on yiyou, he also served as Minister of Education in his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Hong was made General of the Central Army and supervisor of the Secretariat. In the sixth month, on yiyou, he also served as Minister of Education while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：宏為將則覆三軍，為臣則涉大逆，高祖貸其死罪可矣。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: As a general Hong ruined three armies; as a minister he touched upon great treason—Emperor Gaozu sparing his death penalty would have sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Guang says: As a general Hong ruined three armies; as a minister he touched upon great treason. Emperor Gaozu sparing his life would have been enough.

sentences.zh: 數旬之間，還為三公，于兄弟之恩誠厚矣，王者之法果安在哉！

translations.literal: Within a few tens of days he was again one of the Three Excellencies—fraternal favor indeed runs deep; where then is the king's law!
translations.idiomatic: Within a few tens of days he was again one of the Three Excellencies. Brotherly favor indeed runs deep—but where, then, is the king's law!

sentences.zh: 初，洛陽有漢所立《三字石經》，雖屢經喪亂而初無損失。

translations.literal: At first, Luoyang had the Han-era Three-Character Stone Classics; though they passed through many devastations they suffered no loss at first.
translations.idiomatic: At first Luoyang held the Han-era Three-Character Stone Classics. Though they passed through many devastations, they at first suffered no loss.

sentences.zh: 及魏馮熙、常伯夫相繼為洛州刺史，毀取以建浮圖精舍，遂大致頹落，所存者委於榛莽，道俗隨意取之。

translations.literal: When Feng Xi and Chang Bofu of Wei successively served as inspector of Luozhou, they destroyed and took the stones to build pagodas and monasteries; thus they largely fell into ruin; what remained was abandoned to brambles and brush, and monks and layfolk took them at will.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Xi and Chang Bofu of Wei successively served as inspector of Luozhou, they broke up the stones to build pagodas and monasteries. The classics largely fell into ruin; what remained was abandoned to brambles, and monks and layfolk took pieces as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 侍中領國子祭酒崔光請遣官守視，命國子博士李郁等補其殘缺，胡太后許之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Superintendent of the Imperial Academy Cui Guang requested officials be sent to guard and oversee the stones; he ordered Academician Li Yu and others to repair the missing and broken portions; Empress Dowager Hu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and Superintendent of the Imperial Academy Cui Guang asked that officials be sent to guard and oversee the stones, and ordered Academician Li Yu and others to repair the missing and broken portions. Empress Dowager Hu approved.

sentences.zh: 會元叉、劉騰作亂，事遂寢。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuan Cha and Liu Teng raised a rebellion; the matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: But Yuan Cha and Liu Teng then raised a rebellion, and the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏河州羌卻鐵忽反，自稱水池王；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Qiang of Hezhou in Wei, Que Tiehu, rebelled and styled himself King of the Water Pool;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Qiang of Hezhou in Wei, Que Tiehu, rebelled and styled himself King of the Water Pool;

sentences.zh: 詔以主客郎源子恭為行台以討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Principal Clerk of Receiving Guests Yuan Zigong a mobile headquarters to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Principal Clerk of Receiving Guests Yuan Zigong mobile headquarters commander to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 子恭至河州，嚴勒州郡及諸軍毋得犯民一物，亦不得輕與賊戰，然後示以威恩，使知悔懼。

translations.literal: When Zigong reached Hezhou, he strictly forbade the prefectures, commanderies, and all armies from harming even one item belonging to the people, and also from rashly engaging the bandits in battle; only then did he display authority and kindness, so they would know remorse and fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Zigong reached Hezhou, he strictly forbade the prefectures, commanderies, and all armies from harming even one thing belonging to the people, and also from rashly engaging the rebels. Only then did he show both authority and kindness, so they would feel remorse and fear.

sentences.zh: 八月，鐵忽等相帥詣子恭降，首尾不及二旬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Tiehu and the rest led one another to Zigong to surrender—from start to finish not even twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Tiehu and the rest led one another to Zigong to surrender—from first to last, less than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 子恭，懷之子也。

translations.literal: Zigong was the son of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong was the son of Huai.

sentences.zh: 魏宦者劉騰，手不解書，而多奸謀，善揣人意。

translations.literal: The Wei eunuch Liu Teng's hands did not understand writing, yet he had many wicked schemes and was skilled at gauging men's minds.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei eunuch Liu Teng could not read, yet he was full of wicked schemes and skilled at reading men's minds.

sentences.zh: 胡太后以其保護之功，累遷至侍中、右光祿大夫，遂干預政事，納賂為人求官，無不效者。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu, for his merit in protecting her, repeatedly promoted him until Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of Splendor; he then intervened in government, accepted bribes to seek office for others—none failed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu, for his merit in protecting her, repeatedly promoted him until he reached Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of Splendor. He then intervened in government, accepting bribes to secure office for others—and none ever failed.

sentences.zh: 河間王琛，簡之子也，為定州刺史，以貪縱著名，及罷州還，太后詔曰：「琛在定州，唯不將中山宮來，自餘無所不致，何可更復敘用！

translations.literal: Prince Chen of Hejian, son of Jian, served as inspector of Dingzhou, famed for greed and license; when he left his post and returned, the empress dowager edicted: "Chen at Dingzhou brought everything except the Zhongshan Palace itself—nothing he did not steal; how can he be employed again!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chen of Hejian, son of Jian, served as inspector of Dingzhou and was famed for greed and license. When he left his post and returned, the empress dowager edicted, "At Dingzhou Chen brought away everything except the Zhongshan Palace itself—there was nothing he did not steal. How can he be employed again!

sentences.zh: 」遂廢於家。

translations.literal: " He was then dismissed and kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then dismissed and kept at home.

sentences.zh: 琛乃求為騰養息，賂騰金寶巨萬計。

translations.literal: Chen then sought to become Liu Teng's adopted heir; he bribed Teng with gold and treasure totaling tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Chen then sought to become Liu Teng's adopted heir and bribed him with gold and treasure amounting to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 騰為之言於太后，得兼都官尚書，出為秦州刺史，會騰疾篤，太后欲及其生而貴之。

translations.literal: Teng spoke for him to the empress dowager; he obtained the concurrent post of Director of Punishments and went out as inspector of Qinzhou; it happened Teng's illness was severe, and the empress dowager wished to honor him while he yet lived.
translations.idiomatic: Teng spoke for him to the empress dowager. Chen obtained the concurrent post of Director of Punishments and went out as inspector of Qinzhou. Teng's illness then grew severe, and the empress dowager wished to honor him while he still lived.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸未朔，以騰為衛將軍，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day of guiwei, Teng was made Guard General and granted Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day of guiwei, Teng was made Guard General and granted Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魏胡太后以天文有變，欲以崇憲高太后當之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu of Wei, because the heavens showed an omen, wished to have Empress Dowager Gao of Chongxian stand in for it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu of Wei, because the heavens showed an omen, wished to have Empress Dowager Gao of Chongxian stand in its place.

sentences.zh: 戊申夜，高太后暴卒；

translations.literal: On the night of wushen, Empress Dowager Gao died suddenly;
translations.idiomatic: On the night of wushen, Empress Dowager Gao died suddenly;

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁卯，以尼禮葬於北邙，謚曰順皇后。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingmao, she was buried at North Mang by nun's rites, posthumously titled Empress Shun.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingmao, she was buried at North Mang by nun's rites and posthumously titled Empress Shun.

sentences.zh: 百官單衣邪巾送至墓所，事訖而除。

translations.literal: All officials in single garments and slanting headcloths escorted her to the tomb; when the rites ended they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: All officials, in single garments and slanting headcloths, escorted her to the tomb; when the rites ended they were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以臨川王宏為司徒。

translations.literal: On yihai, Prince Hong of Linchuan was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Prince Hong of Linchuan was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 魏胡太后遣使者宋雲與比丘惠生如西域求佛經。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu of Wei sent the envoy Song Yun and the bhikṣu Huisheng to the Western Regions to seek Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu of Wei sent the envoy Song Yun and the monk Huisheng to the Western Regions to seek Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 司空任城王澄奏：「昔高祖遷都，制城內唯聽置僧尼寺各一，餘皆置於城外；

translations.literal: Situ Prince Cheng of Ren Cheng submitted: "Formerly the Great Ancestor moved the capital and decreed that within the city only one monk temple and one nun temple were permitted—the rest all placed outside the walls;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Prince Cheng of Ren Cheng submitted: "Formerly the Great Ancestor moved the capital and decreed that within the city only one monk temple and one nun temple were permitted—all the rest placed outside the walls;

sentences.zh: 蓋以道俗殊歸，欲其淨居塵外故也。

translations.literal: This was because clergy and laity belong to different paths—he wished them to dwell purely beyond the dust.
translations.idiomatic: This was because clergy and laity follow different paths—he wished them to dwell purely beyond the dust of the world.

sentences.zh: 正始三年，沙門統惠深，始違前禁，自是卷詔不行，私謁彌眾，都城之中，寺逾五百，佔奪民居，三分且一，屠沽塵穢，連比雜居。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengshi, Superintendent of Monks Huishen first violated the prior prohibition; from then imperial edicts rolled up went unenforced, private visits multiplied, and within the capital city temples exceeded five hundred, seizing commoners' dwellings—a third or so—butchers and taverns filthy and coarse, adjoining one another in mixed residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengshi, Superintendent of Monks Huishen first violated the prior prohibition. From then on edicts went unenforced and private visits multiplied. Within the capital temples exceeded five hundred, seizing commoners' dwellings—a third of the city or so. Butchers and taverns, filthy and coarse, stood wall to wall with monasteries in mixed habitation.

sentences.zh: 往者代北有法秀之謀，冀州有大乘之變。

translations.literal: In the past in northern Dai there was Fa Xiu's conspiracy; in Jizhou the Mahayana uprising.
translations.idiomatic: In the past northern Dai saw Fa Xiu's conspiracy; Jizhou saw the Mahayana uprising.

sentences.zh: 太和、景明之制，非徒使錙素殊途，蓋亦以防微杜漸。

translations.literal: The regulations of Tahe and Jingming were not merely to keep clergy and laity on different paths—they also served to guard against small beginnings and stop gradual spread.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations of Tahe and Jingming were not merely to keep clergy and laity apart—they also served to guard against small beginnings and stop trouble before it spread.

sentences.zh: 昔如來闡教，多依山林，今此僧徒，戀著城邑，正以誘於利慾，不能自已，此乃釋氏之糟糠，法王之社鼠，內戒所不容，國曲所共棄也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Tathāgata spread the teaching relying mostly on mountains and forests; today's monks cling to cities and towns precisely because enticed by profit and desire they cannot restrain themselves—this is the dregs of the Buddhist lineage, the temple mice of the Dharma King; inner precepts cannot tolerate it, state law jointly abandons it.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Tathāgata spread the teaching chiefly from mountains and forests; today's monks cling to cities and towns because profit and desire entice them and they cannot restrain themselves. These are the dregs of the Buddhist lineage, the temple mice of the Dharma King—what inner precepts cannot tolerate and state law must cast out.

sentences.zh: 臣謂都城內寺未成可徙者，宜悉徙於郭外，僧不滿五十者，並小從大；

translations.literal: Your subject holds that temples within the capital not yet finished and capable of relocation should all be moved outside the outer wall; where monks number fewer than fifty, small ones should merge into large ones;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that temples within the capital not yet finished and capable of relocation should all be moved outside the outer wall; where monks number fewer than fifty, smaller temples should merge into larger ones;

sentences.zh: 外州亦准此。

translations.literal: outer provinces should follow this standard as well.
translations.idiomatic: outer provinces should follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之，然卒不能行。

translations.literal: " An edict approved, yet in the end it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved, yet in the end it could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏太師雍等奏：「鹽池天藏，資育群生，先朝為之禁限，亦非苟與細民爭利。

translations.literal: That year, Grand Preceptor Yong and others of Wei submitted: "The salt ponds are heaven's storehouse, nourishing all living beings; the former dynasty set prohibitions and limits on them—not to contend for profit with common folk in haste.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Grand Preceptor Yong and others of Wei submitted: "The salt ponds are heaven's storehouse, nourishing all living beings. The former dynasty set prohibitions and limits on them—not to grasp at profit with common folk in haste.

sentences.zh: 但利起天池，取用無法，或豪貴封護，或近民吝守，貧弱遠來，邈然絕望。

translations.literal: Yet profit arose at the celestial pond; taking and using lacked law—sometimes noble magnates sealed and guarded them, sometimes nearby folk stingily held them; the poor and weak coming from afar looked across in vain despair.
translations.idiomatic: Yet profit arose at the celestial pond, and taking and using lacked proper law. Sometimes noble magnates sealed and guarded the ponds; sometimes nearby folk hoarded them stingily. The poor and weak coming from afar looked across in vain despair.

sentences.zh: 因置主司，令其裁察，強弱相兼，務令得所。

translations.literal: Therefore a chief office was established to examine and judge, blending strong and weak, striving that all obtain their due.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a chief office was established to examine and judge, balancing strong and weak, striving that all obtain their due.

sentences.zh: 什一之稅，自古有之，所務者遠近齊平，公私兩宜耳。

translations.literal: The one-tenth tax has existed since antiquity; what matters is equal fairness near and far, benefit to public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: The one-tenth tax has existed since antiquity. What matters is equal fairness near and far, benefit to public and private alike.

sentences.zh: 及甄琛啟求罷禁，乃為繞池之民尉保光等擅自固護；

translations.literal: When Zhen Chen memorialized asking to abolish the prohibition, it was for the people around the pond, Wei Baoguang and others, who on their own sealed and guarded it;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen Chen memorialized asking to abolish the prohibition, it was for the people around the pond—Wei Baoguang and others—who on their own sealed and guarded it;

sentences.zh: 語其障禁，倍於官司，取與自由，貴賤任口。

translations.literal: speaking of their barriers and bans, they doubled those of official offices—taking and giving as they pleased, high and low at their word.
translations.idiomatic: Their barriers and bans doubled those of official offices; they took and gave as they pleased, fixing prices as high or low as they liked.

sentences.zh: 請依先朝禁之為便。

translations.literal: We ask that the former dynasty's prohibition be followed—for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the former dynasty's prohibition be restored—for that would be best.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved.
